Accountable obligation owner.value: Controller owns the annual ICFR assessment and signs the management report; day-to-day execution delegated to the SOX Program Manager, conclusion presented to the CFO before certification

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - SOX 404(a) and 302(a)(6) (15 U.S.C. 7262(a), 7241(a)(6)), Reg S-K Item 308(a)/(c) (17 CFR 229.308) and Exchange Act Rule 13a-15(c)-(d) re-read from eCFR at scoping kickoff, together with SEC Interpretive Release 33-8810 on the period-end financial reporting process

In-scope processes.value: Every financial statement cycle feeding the consolidated 10-K: premium and unearned premium, claims and loss reserves, reinsurance ceded, investments and impairment, commissions, treasury, payroll, tax, close and consolidation, plus the entity-level and period-end financial reporting process controls

In-scope systems.value: AuditBoard SOXHUB holds the risk-and-control matrix, walkthroughs and test evidence; in-scope source systems are the general ledger, the policy administration and claims platforms, the reserving models and the close/consolidation tool, each with its ITGC layer

Compliance procedure documented.value: ICFR Assessment Procedure - scoping by quantitative coverage and qualitative risk, RCM maintenance, walkthrough standard, design and operating effectiveness evidence rules, roll-forward from interim to 31 December, deficiency evaluation and the management report

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Controller and the CFO, presented to the Audit Committee at the Q1 SOX planning meeting, and re-approved whenever scope, an acquisition or an ERP change alters the control population

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Assessment is as of 31 December fiscal year-end; scoping approved by 31 March, walkthroughs complete by 30 June, interim testing by 30 September, roll-forward and conclusion by mid-February so the Item 308(a) report is in the 10-K filed within 60 days of year-end for a large accelerated filer

Deadline reminders configured.value: AuditBoard milestone alerts at scoping approval, walkthrough completion, interim cut, roll-forward cut and conclusion date, with weekly ageing reminders to each control owner for open evidence requests

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Scoping memo, RCM, walkthroughs, test workpapers, deficiency evaluations, sub-certifications and the signed management report retained 7 years under Exchange Act Rule 17a-4 style policy, with audit-relevant records held under SOX 802 (18 U.S.C. 1520) for 7 years from the end of the audit period

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every failed control attribute is raised as an issue with severity (deficiency, significant deficiency, material weakness), root cause, owner and remediation date, and is carried in the deficiency log until re-tested

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs the final ICFR conclusion and the aggregate deficiency evaluation; the Audit Committee chair acknowledges any significant deficiency or material weakness before the 10-K is filed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All key controls in the year-end RCM across in-scope entities and cycles, including entity-level, period-end financial reporting process and ITGC controls, with the account coverage schedule that supports them

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Control coverage of at least 80 percent of consolidated total revenue, total assets and pre-tax income; any key control with a design gap or a test failure that is not remediated and re-tested before 31 December fails; one unremediated material weakness makes the ICFR conclusion not effective

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The assertion is annual as of 31 December, so independent validation runs on the same cycle: scope challenge in Q1, design re-performance at interim, and a roll-forward re-test in Q4 covering the period from the interim cut to year-end

Evidence location for test results.value: AuditBoard project ICFR-FY under the year-end assessment folder, cross-linked to the compliance evidence repository record holding the signed management report and the CFO sign-off

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Scoping memo with coverage percentages, the RCM, walkthrough documents, test workpapers, deficiency evaluation and the signed Item 308(a) report, producible to the SEC staff or PCAOB inspectors within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: SEC comment letters on Item 308 disclosure route to the Controller and Regulatory Counsel with Investor Relations, the CFO clears the response and the Audit Committee is briefed before it is filed as correspondence on EDGAR

checklist.step: Set the ICFR scope from the year-end trial balance
actions: Pull the prior-year audited trial balance by legal entity from the general ledger and paste it into the scoping workbook with columns for revenue, total assets and pre-tax income.
Ask the Controller for planning materiality and set the account scoping threshold at the agreed fraction of it, recording both numbers on the cover sheet.

Mark every account above the threshold in scope and every account below it that carries a qualitative risk flag (loss reserves, reinsurance recoverables, deferred acquisition costs, investment impairment, related-party balances).
Compute and record the coverage percentage of consolidated revenue, assets and pre-tax income obtained by the in-scope accounts.
Send the draft scope to the Controller and the external audit engagement team for challenge before it is frozen.
checklist.done: the scoping workbook shows account-level in/out decisions with computed coverage percentages against revenue, assets and pre-tax income.

checklist.step: Rank locations and business units by risk and lock the entity scope
actions: List every consolidated legal entity, writing company and shared service centre with its contribution to each in-scope account.
Score each location for inherent risk: acquisitions in the last 24 months, ERP or policy administration migrations, prior-year deficiencies, manual close activity, offshore processing.
Classify each location as full-scope, specific-scope (named accounts only) or out-of-scope, and write the reason on the row.
Have the Controller approve the location scope in writing and file the approval with the scoping memo.
checklist.done: each entity carries a documented full/specific/out-of-scope classification with a stated reason and a Controller approval.

checklist.step: Refresh the process narrative and flowchart for each in-scope cycle
actions: Book a walkthrough session with each process owner (Senior Accountant for close, Reserving Actuary for loss reserves, Reinsurance Accountant for ceded) and take the transaction from initiation to the general ledger posting.
Update the narrative in AuditBoard to name the systems touched, the reports used, the approval points and the people who perform each step.
Redraw the flowchart to show every hand-off between systems, marking where data leaves the system of record into a spreadsheet.
Record what changed since last year (new system, new outsourcer, new product) in the change log at the head of the narrative.
checklist.done: each in-scope cycle has a current-year narrative and flowchart with a dated change log and a named process owner.

checklist.step: Build the risk-and-control matrix down to assertion level
actions: For each in-scope account list the what-can-go-wrong statements and map them to the assertions: existence, completeness, valuation, rights and obligations, presentation.
Attach at least one control to every assertion and record for each control the control id, owner, frequency, type (preventive/detective, manual/automated), and whether it is a key control.
For management review controls record the review threshold, the precision of the investigation trigger and the source of the report reviewed.
Flag every control that relies on a system-generated report or a spreadsheet, and register the report or end-user computing file for completeness and accuracy testing.
Have the process owner attest in AuditBoard that the matrix reflects how the work is actually performed.
checklist.done: every in-scope assertion has at least one owned key control in the RCM, with review precision and report/EUC dependencies recorded.

checklist.step: Scope the IT general controls that the automated controls depend on
actions: List every application, database and operating system supporting an in-scope automated control, key report or interface, and confirm each one has a named application owner.

For each layer document the ITGC set: user access provisioning and removal, periodic user access review, privileged access, change management approval and migration segregation, and batch job monitoring.
In SailPoint IGA export the current entitlement catalogue for each in-scope application and confirm a certification campaign is scheduled at least semi-annually.
Hand the ITGC control list to the SOX Program Manager for inclusion in the RCM and note any application with no owner as an immediate design gap.
checklist.done: every in-scope application layer has documented access, change and operations ITGCs with a named owner and a scheduled access certification.

checklist.step: Cover outsourced processing with SOC 1 reports and complementary controls
actions: List every service organisation touching in-scope data: third-party administrators, claims bill review, investment custodians and accounting agents, payroll and actuarial outsourcers.
Obtain each provider's current SOC 1 Type 2 report and check the period covered ends inside the fiscal year; where a gap exists request a bridge letter covering the stub period to 31 December.
Read the report for qualified opinions and exceptions, and extract the complementary user entity controls into the RCM as controls the company must perform itself.
Assign an owner and a test step to every complementary user entity control and notify the SOX Program Manager where a provider will not supply a SOC 1.
checklist.done: each service organisation has a current SOC 1 Type 2 plus a bridge letter to year-end, and its complementary user entity controls sit in the RCM with owners.

checklist.step: Walk through every key control and prove it exists as described
actions: Select one live transaction per key control and follow it end to end with the performer, watching the control being executed rather than accepting a description.
Capture the evidence the control leaves behind: the signed reconciliation, the system approval record, the exception report with the follow-up note.
For management review controls ask what threshold triggers investigation and get an example of an item actually investigated and resolved.
Load the walkthrough document, screenshots and source report into the AuditBoard control record and date it.
checklist.done: every key control has a dated walkthrough with an observed execution, retained evidence and a review-precision example.

checklist.step: Conclude on design effectiveness before any operating testing starts
actions: For each assertion ask whether the mapped controls, executed as designed, would prevent or detect a material misstatement, and write the answer on the RCM row.
Raise a design gap where a risk has no control, where the review precision cannot catch a material amount, or where the performer also approves their own work.
Log each design gap in AuditBoard with the account, the assertion, the potential magnitude and a remediation owner and date.
Hold operating effectiveness testing on any control with an open design gap until the redesigned control is in place, and record the date the new control started operating.
checklist.done: each assertion has a written design conclusion and every design gap has a logged owner, date and start-of-operation date for the replacement control.

checklist.step: Evidence operating effectiveness across the year
actions: Set the sample size from the control frequency using the standard table: annual 1, quarterly 2, monthly 2 to 5, weekly 5 to 15, daily 20 to 40, many-times-daily 25 to 60, with automated controls tested once plus supporting ITGCs.
Issue the evidence requests through the AuditBoard PBC list with a named control owner and a due date, and chase items ageing beyond 5 business days.
Test each item against the written attributes (performed, performed timely, evidence of review, exception followed to resolution) and record pass or fail per attribute, never per control overall.
Where an attribute fails, extend the sample or conclude the control is not effective, and open a deficiency rather than re-selecting a cleaner sample.
checklist.done: each key control has a completed test with frequency-appropriate sample size, attribute-level results and evidence attached in AuditBoard.

checklist.step: Assess the period-end financial reporting process controls
actions: Document the close as SEC Release 33-8810 defines it: journal entry initiation and approval, consolidation and eliminations, intercompany settlement, top-side and out-of-system adjustments, and the drafting of the statements and footnotes.
In BlackLine confirm every balance sheet reconciliation in scope is assigned, certified by the preparer and approved by an independent reviewer within the close calendar day count.
Test that manual journal entries above the posting threshold carry a second approver who did not prepare the entry, and pull the list of entries posted after the close cut-off for review.
Test the controls over the disclosure checklist and the tie-out of the draft 10-K to the general ledger and supporting schedules.
checklist.done: close, consolidation, journal entry approval and statement tie-out controls are documented and tested with evidence in BlackLine and the close file.

checklist.step: Roll interim testing forward to the year-end assertion date
actions: List every control tested before 30 September and record the number of days between the interim cut and 31 December.
For each, ask the control owner in writing whether the control, the performer or the system changed after the interim date and file the reply.
Test additional roll-forward samples for high-risk controls and for any control where something changed, sized to the remaining period.
Record the roll-forward conclusion on the control row so the year-end assertion rests on evidence covering the full period.
checklist.done: every interim-tested control shows a roll-forward inquiry, any change-driven additional testing, and a conclusion as of 31 December.

checklist.step: Collect sub-certifications from process and entity owners
actions: Issue the sub-certification questionnaire through DocuSign to every in-scope process owner, entity controller and shared service lead in the first week of January.

Require each signer to affirm control performance for their area, disclose any control failure, override, unrecorded liability or fraud allegation, and confirm all significant estimates were escalated.
Track returns to 100 percent and escalate any signer outstanding more than 5 business days to the CFO.
Read every qualified answer, follow it to the underlying facts with the signer and record the resolution in the assessment file.
checklist.done: all sub-certifications are returned and signed, and every disclosed exception is investigated with a documented resolution.

checklist.step: Evaluate deficiencies in aggregate and reach the ICFR conclusion
actions: Gather every open deficiency from the AuditBoard log, including deficiencies raised by the external auditor and by the sub-certification process.
For each, estimate the magnitude of potential misstatement against materiality and judge the likelihood, then classify as deficiency, significant deficiency or material weakness.
Group deficiencies affecting the same account or assertion and re-evaluate them in aggregate, because individually small items can combine into a material weakness.
Discuss the classification with the external audit partner and the Chief Audit Executive before it is finalised, and record where views differ and how it was settled.
Write the conclusion - effective, or not effective with the material weakness described - and take it to the CFO and the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: every deficiency is classified individually and in aggregate, discussed with the external auditor, and a written ICFR conclusion is signed by the CFO.

checklist.step: Draft management's report on ICFR and the Item 308(c) change disclosure
actions: Draft the Item 308(a) report stating management's responsibility, naming COSO 2013 as the framework used, giving the assessment date of 31 December and the conclusion on effectiveness.
Where the conclusion is not effective, describe the material weakness and its remediation plan and confirm the conclusion cannot be qualified as effective with exceptions.

Draft the Item 308(c) disclosure of any change in ICFR during the fourth quarter that materially affected or is reasonably likely to materially affect ICFR, drawing on the change log and the roll-forward inquiries.
Circulate both to the Disclosure Committee and the external auditor, then file the final text into the 10-K working file in the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: the Item 308(a) report and the Item 308(c) fourth-quarter change disclosure are drafted, framework-named, and cleared by the Disclosure Committee.

checklist.step: Close and retain the assessment file
actions: Lock the AuditBoard project for the year so no workpaper can be edited after the conclusion date, and export the full evidence set.
File the scoping memo, RCM, walkthroughs, test workpapers, deficiency evaluation, sub-certifications and signed management report into the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year.
Apply the 7-year retention label required for audit-period records under SOX 802 and confirm no deletion job can reach the folder.
Confirm the index makes the record searchable by control id, account, entity and fiscal year, and hand the access list to the Chief Audit Executive.
checklist.done: the locked assessment file is in the evidence repository under a 7-year retention label and is searchable by control id and entity.

testing.step: Build the population of key controls supporting the assertion
actions: Export from AuditBoard every control flagged key in the year-end RCM with entity, cycle, account, assertion, frequency, type and owner.
Add entity-level, period-end financial reporting and ITGC controls so no control category is silently excluded.
Compare the control count and cycle mix to the prior year and get a written explanation for any cycle whose key control count moved more than 10 percent.
Sign the population as complete and record the extract date and record count in the workpaper.
testing.done: a dated, signed key-control population is extracted and reconciled to the prior year with explanations for material movement.

testing.step: Reconcile the scope back to the audited trial balance
actions: Pull the consolidated trial balance from the general ledger and independently recompute the coverage percentages of revenue, total assets and pre-tax income claimed in the scoping memo.
Identify every account above the stated threshold that was scoped out and read the documented rationale for each one.
Check that loss reserves, reinsurance recoverables and investment valuation are in scope regardless of the quantitative threshold, given their estimation risk.
Record any coverage figure below the 80 percent threshold as an exception in its own right.
testing.done: coverage percentages are independently recomputed and every above-threshold exclusion has a rationale on file.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample of controls
actions: Take 100 percent of controls over loss reserves, reinsurance and the period-end financial reporting process.
Take 30 further controls by seeded random selection across the remaining population, stratified so every in-scope entity contributes at least one.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Add every control that failed or was remediated in the prior year as a mandatory sample item.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible from the recorded seed, and covers all reserve, reinsurance, close and prior-year-failed controls.

testing.step: Re-perform design assessment on the sampled controls
actions: Read the risk statement and assertion for each sampled control and reach an independent design conclusion before opening management's assessment.
Re-walk one transaction per sampled control with the performer and confirm the narrative matches the observed execution.
Challenge management review controls on precision: ask what amount would have had to move before the reviewer would have questioned it, and compare that to materiality.
Record every difference from management's design conclusion as an exception, including cases where the conclusion is right but the documented rationale is wrong.
testing.done: each sampled control has an independent design conclusion with an observed re-walk and a precision challenge for review controls.

testing.step: Re-perform operating effectiveness tests and check sample sizing
actions: For each sampled control recompute the required sample size from its stated frequency and compare it to the number of items management actually tested.
Re-select 3 items per control independently from the source system population rather than from management's selection sheet, and test them against the documented attributes.
Confirm each item of evidence carries a date and a performer identity, and reject evidence generated after the test request as not contemporaneous.
Flag any control where management passed a control despite a failed attribute or replaced a failed sample item.
testing.done: sample sizes are recomputed against frequency and independently reselected items pass every documented attribute, or an exception is raised.

testing.step: Test the ITGC and access foundation under the automated controls
actions: For each in-scope application pull the current entitlement export from SailPoint IGA and reconcile privileged account holders to an approved privileged access list.
Take 10 leavers from the HR termination report and confirm application access was revoked within the policy window, recording the actual day count for each.
Take 10 production changes from the change management record and confirm approval before migration and that the developer did not migrate their own change.
Conclude explicitly on whether an ITGC failure undermines any automated control or system-generated report relied on elsewhere in the assessment.
testing.done: privileged access, leaver revocation day counts and change segregation are tested, with a stated impact on dependent automated controls.

testing.step: Recompute the roll-forward maths and evidence period coverage
actions: For 10 interim-tested controls recompute the days between the interim test cut and 31 December and compare to the roll-forward procedure performed.
Confirm a written change inquiry exists from the control owner and that additional testing was performed wherever a change was disclosed.
Check that the evidence tested spans the full fiscal year for controls operating throughout it, and that no control asserts effectiveness on evidence from a single quarter.
Log any control whose evidence stops before year-end without a roll-forward conclusion as an exception.
testing.done: roll-forward day counts are recomputed and every interim-tested control has period coverage to 31 December or a logged exception.

testing.step: Trace sub-certifications and the deficiency evaluation into the conclusion
actions: Reconcile the DocuSign sub-certification return list to the in-scope entity and process owner list and identify anyone who never signed.
Read every qualified sub-certification answer and trace it to a logged deficiency or a documented resolution.
Recalculate the aggregate deficiency evaluation: confirm deficiencies touching the same account or assertion were combined and re-assessed, not evaluated only in isolation.
Compare the final conclusion wording to the classification worksheet and confirm no material weakness was reported as a significant deficiency.
testing.done: every sub-certification is accounted for, each qualification traces to a disposition, and the aggregate deficiency maths supports the stated conclusion.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one AuditBoard issue per exception naming the control id, entity, what failed and the potential misstatement magnitude.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (scoping omission, stale documentation, insufficient review precision, evidence not retained, ITGC failure, resourcing) and name a single accountable owner.
Set a remediation date that leaves a sufficient period of operating effectiveness before the next 31 December assertion date, and record the number of operating cycles needed for re-testing.
Carry every open issue into the next assessment as a mandatory test item and report unremediated prior-year issues separately to the Audit Committee.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a re-test cycle count that fits before the next assertion date.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Audit Committee
actions: Compute the exception rate over the sample and compare it to the stated threshold of zero unremediated key control failures.
Write the conclusion - the management ICFR assessment is supported, supported with exceptions, or not supported - and reference the workpaper evidence behind each element.
Have the reviewer, who owned, performed or documented none of the sampled controls, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Present results, unremediated deficiencies and any disagreement with management to the Audit Committee before the 10-K is filed and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception rate, the conclusion and the Audit Committee reporting date, filed before the 10-K is filed.

checklist.step: Write the quarterly test plan from the current control matrix
actions: Export the key control list from the AuditBoard RCM and mark which controls fall due for testing this quarter based on their frequency and last test date.
Add every control that failed in a prior quarter, every newly designed control and every control affected by a system or process change reported by the control owner.
Set the test period start and end dates for each control so that, across the four quarters, evidence covers the full fiscal year to 31 December.
Send the plan to the Chief Audit Executive and the external audit engagement team and record their reliance requests so testing can be leveraged rather than duplicated.
checklist.done: the quarterly plan names every control due, prior failures and change-driven retests, with test periods that combine to full-year coverage.

checklist.step: Set sample sizes from control frequency and population
actions: For each control read its frequency from the RCM and apply the standard table: annual 1, quarterly 2, monthly 2 to 5, weekly 5 to 15, daily 20 to 40, many-times-daily 25 to 60.
Extract the actual population for the period from the source system (journal entries posted, reconciliations completed, claims approved) and record the population count on the test sheet.
Increase the sample where the control is higher risk, failed last year, or was performed by more than one person during the period, and record the reason for the increase.
For automated controls plan a single test of one instance plus explicit reliance on the change management and access ITGCs for the application.
checklist.done: each control has a documented population count, a frequency-based sample size and a written reason for any increase.

checklist.step: Issue evidence requests and chase them to completion
actions: Raise a PBC request in AuditBoard per control naming the exact artifact wanted (the December bank reconciliation with the preparer and reviewer stamps, the reserve committee minutes, the SQL query and its parameters), the owner and a due date.
Require system-generated reports to be delivered with the run parameters, run date and user id visible so completeness and accuracy can be tested.
Chase requests ageing beyond 5 business days and escalate at 10 business days to the process owner's director.
Reject evidence created after the request date as not contemporaneous and record the fact on the control row.
checklist.done: every planned control has contemporaneous evidence attached with report parameters visible, or a documented escalation.

checklist.step: Test the completeness and accuracy of every report the control relies on
actions: For each system-generated report used by a control, obtain the report logic or query and confirm the filters and date ranges match the control's stated scope.
Reconcile the report totals to the general ledger balance or to a system control total, and record both figures and the difference.
Trace 5 items from the report back to the source record and 5 source records forward into the report to test both accuracy and completeness.
Register any spreadsheet used in the control as an end-user computing file and test its formulas, access restrictions and version control.
checklist.done: each report used by a control is reconciled to a system total with two-way tracing performed and any spreadsheet registered and tested.

checklist.step: Execute the tests attribute by attribute
actions: Record for each sample item whether the control was performed, performed within the required timeframe, evidenced by an identifiable reviewer, and whether exceptions the control found were followed to resolution.
Mark pass or fail at attribute level, never a single overall verdict, and write what was inspected for each attribute.
Where a reviewer signature exists but no investigation trail does, fail the review-precision attribute rather than accepting the signature as evidence.
Attach the tested artifact to the sample row in AuditBoard so the conclusion can be re-performed by someone else.
checklist.done: each sample item shows attribute-level pass or fail with the inspected artifact attached.

checklist.step: Confirm the failure with the control owner before classifying it
actions: Send the draft exception to the control owner with the item id, date, what was tested and what was missing, and give 3 business days to respond.
Accept additional contemporaneous evidence only where it is dated at the time of the original control performance, and record why it was not produced initially.
Where the owner cannot produce evidence, confirm the exception in writing and close the discussion - a control with no evidence did not operate for testing purposes.
Log the confirmed exception in the AuditBoard deficiency log with the account, assertion and the transaction volume and value flowing through the control.
checklist.done: each exception is confirmed in writing with the owner and logged with the account, assertion and exposed transaction volume.

checklist.step: Estimate the magnitude of potential misstatement for each deficiency
actions: For each deficiency compute the gross exposure: the value of transactions or the balance the control was designed to protect during the failure period, not just the value of the failed sample items.
Compare that exposure to planning materiality and to the significant deficiency threshold agreed with the external auditor, and record both comparisons.
Identify any compensating control operating at a precision able to catch the same misstatement, test it, and only then reduce the assessed magnitude.
Write a one-page magnitude memo per deficiency showing the exposure figure, the compensating control tested, and the residual exposure.
checklist.done: each deficiency has a magnitude memo with the exposed balance, the materiality comparison and any tested compensating control.

checklist.step: Classify each deficiency by severity under the Release 33-8810 framework
actions: Assess likelihood as remote, reasonably possible or probable, and combine it with the magnitude to reach a severity of deficiency, significant deficiency or material weakness.

Apply the strong indicators of a material weakness directly: identified fraud by senior management, restatement of previously issued statements, a material misstatement found by the auditor and not by the controls, and ineffective oversight by the audit committee.
Group deficiencies affecting the same account or assertion and re-classify the group, since several individually minor items can combine into a material weakness.
Agree the classification with the external audit partner and record any difference of view and how it was resolved.
checklist.done: every deficiency and deficiency group carries a documented likelihood, magnitude and severity, agreed with the external auditor.

checklist.step: Build a remediation plan with a named owner and a dated milestone set
actions: For each deficiency name a single accountable owner at director level or above - not a shared team - and record the root cause from the fixed list.
Write the remediation steps: redesign the control, add a preventive system edit, split the duty, retrain the performer, or move the activity to an automated control.
Set the date the remediated control will begin operating and count forward the number of operating cycles needed before it can be re-tested with a sufficient period of evidence.
Where the remediation cannot deliver enough operating cycles before 31 December, say so in the plan and record the consequence for the year-end assertion instead of hiding it.
checklist.done: each deficiency has a named senior owner, a root cause, a start-of-operation date and a stated operating-cycle count before re-test.

checklist.step: Track remediation to completion week by week
actions: Maintain the remediation dashboard in AuditBoard showing every open item with severity, owner, due date and days overdue.
Hold a fortnightly remediation call with the Controller and each owner with an item due in the next 60 days and minute the status changes.
Escalate any item more than 30 days overdue to the CFO and any significant deficiency or material weakness item to the Audit Committee chair.
Refuse date extensions that push a re-test past the point where two operating cycles fit before year-end without an explicit CFO decision recorded on the item.
checklist.done: the remediation dashboard is current, overdue items are escalated on the stated thresholds and every date extension carries a recorded decision.

checklist.step: Re-test the remediated control over a sufficient period
actions: Confirm the redesigned control is documented in the RCM with its new frequency, performer and evidence, and that the narrative was updated.
Re-test only over the period after the remediation start date, sizing the sample to the new frequency, and never carry forward pre-remediation evidence.
For a monthly control require at least two post-remediation months of evidence; for a quarterly control require at least one full post-remediation quarter plus corroborating design evidence.
Have the re-test performed by an auditor who did not design the remediation, and record their name on the workpaper.
checklist.done: each remediated control has a post-remediation re-test with a frequency-appropriate sample and an independent tester named.

checklist.step: Close deficiencies only on evidence, and re-open on failure
actions: Review the re-test workpaper before closing any item and confirm the sample sits entirely inside the post-remediation period.
Close the item in AuditBoard with the re-test reference, the closing date and the reviewer name, and never close on a management assertion alone.
Where the re-test fails, re-open the deficiency at the same or higher severity, restart the remediation clock and notify the Controller and the external auditor the same week.
Report any deficiency open for more than two consecutive quarters to the Audit Committee as a repeat finding.
checklist.done: no deficiency is closed without a post-remediation re-test reference, and failed re-tests are re-opened with the clock restarted.

checklist.step: Report the quarterly deficiency position to the Audit Committee
actions: Prepare the quarterly SOX report showing controls tested, pass rate, new deficiencies by severity, open items by age and repeat findings.
Name every significant deficiency and material weakness with its owner, remediation date and whether it will be remediated in time for the year-end assertion.
Post the report to the board portal at least 5 business days before the Audit Committee meeting and take questions in executive session without management present.
Record the committee's directions in the minutes and convert each direction into a tracked action with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: the committee has a distributed quarterly deficiency report, an executive session record and tracked actions from its directions.

checklist.step: Feed the quarterly result into the Rule 13a-15(d) change evaluation
actions: List the changes in internal control over financial reporting during the quarter: new controls from remediation, system migrations, outsourcing changes, organisational moves.
Assess whether each change materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, ICFR, and write the reasoning.
Give the assessment and the open deficiency list to the Disclosure Committee for the Item 4 disclosure in the 10-Q and the Item 308(c) disclosure in the 10-K.
Confirm the certifying officers were briefed on every significant deficiency and material weakness before they signed the 302 certifications.
checklist.done: each quarter has a written ICFR change evaluation feeding the periodic report disclosure, with certifying officers briefed on all open severe deficiencies.

checklist.step: Archive the quarter's testing and remediation evidence
actions: Lock the AuditBoard quarterly project after the Audit Committee report so workpapers cannot be edited retrospectively.
Export the test workpapers, deficiency log, magnitude memos, remediation plans and re-test evidence and file them into the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year and quarter.
Apply the 7-year retention label and confirm the record is searchable by control id, deficiency id, severity and owner.
Give the external audit team read access to the archived quarter so their reliance testing works from the same records.
checklist.done: the locked quarterly file is archived under a 7-year label, searchable by deficiency id, and readable by the external auditor.

testing.step: Build the population of tests performed and deficiencies raised
actions: Export from AuditBoard every control test completed in the quarter with control id, tester, sample size, attribute results and conclusion.
Export the full deficiency log including items raised by the external auditor, by control owner self-identification and by prior quarters still open.
Reconcile the tested control list to the approved quarterly test plan and list every planned control that was not tested, with the stated reason.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and record counts.
testing.done: tested controls and deficiencies are extracted, reconciled to the approved plan and signed as complete with untested controls listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the deficiency log to independent failure sources
actions: Compare the deficiency log to the external auditor's summary of audit differences and control observations and identify anything the log is missing.
Compare it to the sub-certification qualifications, the whistleblower log and the journal entry override report and confirm each potential control failure was assessed.
List any failure known to another source but absent from the log as an automatic exception in completeness of the deficiency population.
Record the reconciled deficiency count that all later sampling will draw from.
testing.done: the deficiency log is reconciled to auditor observations, sub-certification qualifications and override reports, with unlogged failures flagged.

testing.step: Select a documented sample of tests and deficiencies
actions: Take 100 percent of significant deficiencies and material weaknesses and 100 percent of items closed in the quarter.
Take 25 completed control tests by seeded random selection, stratified across cycles so reserves, ceded reinsurance and close each contribute.
Add every repeat finding open for more than two quarters as a mandatory item.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all severe and closed deficiencies, all repeat findings and a stratified selection of completed tests.

testing.step: Re-perform sample sizing and attribute testing on sampled controls
actions: Recompute the required sample size from the control frequency and the extracted population and compare it to what was tested.
Independently reselect 3 items per sampled control from the source system population and test them against the documented attributes without reading the original results first.
Compare your attribute conclusions to the tester's and treat any difference as an exception, including a control passed despite a failed attribute.
Check that no sample item was replaced after selection and that the selection evidence retains the original list.
testing.done: sample sizes are recomputed and independently reselected items are re-tested with differences logged, including any post-selection replacement.

testing.step: Re-perform the severity classification on every sampled deficiency
actions: Read the magnitude memo and reach your own likelihood and magnitude conclusion before reading the assigned severity.
Check the exposure figure was computed on the balance or transaction volume the control protected during the whole failure period, not on the failed sample items alone.
Confirm any compensating control credited in the memo was itself tested in the period and operates at sufficient precision.
Test whether deficiencies affecting the same account or assertion were aggregated, and re-classify the group yourself where they were not.
testing.done: each sampled deficiency has an independent severity conclusion with exposure recomputed and aggregation re-performed.

testing.step: Verify remediation evidence and re-test independence
actions: For each closed deficiency open the re-test workpaper and confirm every sampled item falls after the recorded remediation start date.
Confirm the RCM and narrative were updated to the redesigned control and that the new evidence type is actually being produced.
Check the re-tester is not the remediation designer and is not the control performer, naming both people in the workpaper.
Treat any closure supported only by a management confirmation email as a fail of the closure process.
testing.done: every closure is supported by post-remediation evidence, an updated RCM and a named independent re-tester.

testing.step: Recompute remediation timing against the year-end assertion date
actions: For each open deficiency compute the number of operating cycles that fit between the planned remediation start date and 31 December at the control's frequency.
Flag every item where fewer than two operating cycles fit, because it cannot support an effective conclusion at year-end.
Compare original due dates to current due dates and list every extension with the recorded approver.
Compute the average age of open deficiencies and the count open more than two quarters, and compare both to the prior quarter.
testing.done: operating cycles to year-end are recomputed for every open item, extensions are listed with approvers and ageing is trended.

testing.step: Test the completeness and accuracy of the evidence relied on in testing
actions: For 10 sampled tests confirm the report used carries visible run parameters, run date and user id, and that a completeness and accuracy test was documented.
Re-run or re-request one report per cycle from the general ledger and reconcile it to the version the tester used, noting any difference.
Confirm every spreadsheet in the sampled evidence is registered as an end-user computing file with access and version controls tested.
Flag any test whose conclusion rests on an unreconciled report as an exception regardless of the attribute results.
testing.done: reports underpinning sampled tests are re-reconciled, EUC files are confirmed registered, and unreconciled evidence is flagged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the control or deficiency id, what was wrong, and whether it affects the reliability of the year-end conclusion.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (under-sampled, evidence not contemporaneous, magnitude understated, aggregation missed, closure without re-test, tester not independent) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date inside the current quarter for process exceptions so the next cycle is clean.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's validation as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a date inside the quarter and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate across re-performed tests and severity re-classifications and compare to the stated zero-tolerance threshold for closures without re-test evidence.
Write the conclusion - the testing and remediation process is effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references behind each element.
Have a reviewer who tested none of the sampled controls and designed none of the remediations sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion, unremediated severe deficiencies and any classification disagreement to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception rate, a conclusion and the committee reporting date, filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Chief Audit Executive administers the auditor independence and pre-approval process on behalf of the Audit Committee; the Corporate Secretary records committee pre-approvals and the Controller controls the fee ledger

checklist.step: Obtain the annual written independence communication from the audit firm
actions: Request the PCAOB Rule 3526 letter from the engagement partner before the engagement is accepted for the new year and annually thereafter.
Check the letter describes in writing all relationships between the firm, its affiliates and the company that may reasonably bear on independence, and affirms the firm is independent under Rule 2-01.
Require the firm to list every network member firm engaged anywhere in the group, including non-US affiliates providing tax or advisory services.
Table the letter at the Audit Committee, minute the discussion of the disclosed relationships and file the signed original with the engagement letter.
checklist.done: a current Rule 3526 letter listing all relationships and network firms is on file and minuted at the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Refresh the prohibited service list against Rule 2-01(c)(4)
actions: Re-read Reg S-X Rule 2-01(c)(4) and list the prohibited services: bookkeeping, financial information systems design and implementation, appraisal or valuation, actuarial services, internal audit outsourcing, management or human resources functions, broker-dealer or investment banking, legal services and expert services unrelated to the audit.
Add the contingent fee and business relationship prohibitions in Rule 2-01(c)(5) and (c)(3) and the tax services restrictions in PCAOB Rules 3521 to 3523.
Translate each prohibition into plain language a business sponsor can apply and publish it in the pre-approval request form.
Circulate the refreshed list to Procurement, Tax, Actuarial and Internal Audit and confirm receipt.
checklist.done: the current prohibited service list is published in the request form and acknowledged by Procurement, Tax and Actuarial.

checklist.step: Set the general pre-approval categories and dollar caps for the year
actions: Draft the annual pre-approval schedule listing permitted service categories - statutory audits, comfort letters, employee benefit plan audits, agreed-upon procedures, tax compliance and tax return preparation - each with a dollar cap and a description detailed enough that management is not making the approval decision.
Take the schedule to the Audit Committee for approval at the first meeting of the fiscal year and record the approval, the caps and the effective period in the minutes.
Post the approved schedule to the board portal and issue the pre-approval id range to Procurement.
Record that any service outside the schedule, or above a cap, needs specific Audit Committee pre-approval before work starts.
checklist.done: an Audit Committee-approved pre-approval schedule with categories, descriptions, caps and an effective period is minuted and issued to Procurement.

checklist.step: Gate every purchase to the audit firm through the pre-approval id
actions: Flag the audit firm and every network member firm as restricted suppliers in the procurement system so no requisition can be submitted without a pre-approval id field completed.
Configure the workflow to route any requisition against a restricted supplier to the Chief Audit Executive for validation before a purchase order is issued.
Block invoice payment where the invoice references a service description that does not match the approved category on the pre-approval record.
Send Internal Audit a monthly report of every requisition, purchase order and invoice against the restricted supplier list.
checklist.done: no purchase order to the audit firm or a network firm can issue without a validated pre-approval id, and monthly activity reports reach Internal Audit.

checklist.step: Run the specific pre-approval route for anything outside the schedule
actions: Require the business sponsor to submit a request stating the service, the deliverable, the fee estimate, the reason the audit firm is best placed, and a written assessment against the prohibited service list.
Ask the engagement partner to confirm in writing the firm can perform the service without impairing independence and to identify any Rule 2-01 issue.
Present the request to the Audit Committee, or to the chair under the delegated authority if the policy permits, and report any delegated approval to the full committee at its next meeting.
Issue the pre-approval id only after the decision is minuted, and never allow work to start on an anticipated approval.
checklist.done: each out-of-schedule service has a sponsor request, an auditor independence confirmation, a minuted decision and an id issued before work started.

checklist.step: Maintain the partner rotation register
actions: Ask the audit firm for the engagement team roster naming the lead engagement partner, the concurring or engagement quality review partner and other audit partners with their first year of service on the engagement.

Record each partner's consecutive years of service and compute the rotation-off year: 5 consecutive years for the lead and concurring partners with a 5-year time-out, 7 years for other audit partners with a 2-year time-out.
Set calendar alerts at 180 and 90 days before a rotation date so the successor partner can shadow the year before the change.
Have the engagement partner confirm the register annually in writing and file the confirmation.
checklist.done: the rotation register shows each partner's start year, consecutive years and rotation-off year, confirmed in writing by the firm.

checklist.step: Enforce the one-year cooling-off period on hires from the audit team
actions: Define in Workday which positions are financial reporting oversight roles: CEO, CFO, Controller, Chief Accounting Officer, Treasurer, and any role with responsibility for the financial statements or their preparation.
Add a mandatory pre-offer check on those requisitions asking whether the candidate was a member of the audit engagement team, and route any yes answer to the Chief Audit Executive.
Where the candidate served on the engagement team, confirm a full annual audit period has elapsed since they last participated before an offer can issue.
Log the assessment against the requisition and notify the engagement partner of any hire from the firm regardless of role.
checklist.done: every financial reporting oversight hire carries a documented cooling-off assessment and the audit firm is notified of all hires from it.

checklist.step: Reconcile fees to pre-approvals each quarter
actions: Extract from the accounts payable ledger every amount paid or accrued to the audit firm and its network firms in the quarter, by legal entity and invoice.
Map each invoice to a pre-approval id and classify the fee as Audit, Audit-Related, Tax or All Other in the proxy fee table categories.
List every unmatched invoice and every invoice whose cumulative spend exceeds its category cap, and hand both lists to the Chief Audit Executive the same week.
Report the cumulative year-to-date fee position, by category and against caps, at each Audit Committee meeting.
checklist.done: every invoice to the audit firm is matched to a pre-approval id and classified into a proxy fee category, with unmatched and over-cap items escalated.

checklist.step: Assess independence for affiliates, plans and joint arrangements
actions: List every entity within the audit client definition in Rule 2-01(f)(4): consolidated subsidiaries, employee benefit plans, investees where the company has significant influence, and entities under common control.
Ask Treasury and Investments whether the audit firm holds any lending, brokerage or business relationship with a covered person or with the company, which Rule 2-01(c)(1) and (c)(3) restrict.
Confirm no partner or covered person of the firm holds a direct or material indirect financial interest in the company, using the firm's annual confirmation.
Record the assessment for each affiliate and flag any new acquisition, joint venture or plan to the engagement partner within 30 days of completion.
checklist.done: every audit client affiliate is assessed for independence and new acquisitions or plans are notified to the audit firm within 30 days.

checklist.step: Publish and maintain the Item 406 code of ethics for senior financial officers
actions: Confirm the code of ethics applies by name to the principal executive officer, principal financial officer, principal accounting officer or controller and persons performing similar functions.

Check the code addresses the Item 406(b) elements: honest and ethical conduct, handling of conflicts of interest, full and fair disclosure in filings, compliance with law, prompt internal reporting of violations and accountability for adherence.
Post the current code on the investor relations section of the corporate website and record the URL, since Item 406(c) allows website posting in place of filing the code as an exhibit.
Collect annual acknowledgements from the covered officers and file them with the governance record.
checklist.done: a current Item 406-compliant code naming the covered officers is posted at a recorded URL with signed annual acknowledgements on file.

checklist.step: Disclose amendments and waivers promptly
actions: Treat any amendment to a provision of the code that applies to a covered officer, and any express or implicit waiver, as a disclosable event.

File a Form 8-K under Item 5.05 within 4 business days of the amendment or waiver, or post it on the website within 4 business days if the company has disclosed its intention to use website disclosure.
Record the nature of the waiver, the name of the officer, the date and the reason it was granted.
Report every waiver request to the Audit Committee before it is granted, whether or not it is ultimately given.
checklist.done: each code amendment or waiver is disclosed within 4 business days by 8-K Item 5.05 or the disclosed website route, and reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Evaluate the audit firm and recommend re-appointment
actions: Run the annual auditor evaluation survey with the CFO, Controller, business unit finance leads and the Audit Committee covering quality, industry expertise in insurance reserving, responsiveness and independence.
Obtain the firm's most recent PCAOB inspection report and its internal quality control review results and read the findings relevant to insurance issuers.
Compile the fee history, the non-audit to audit fee ratio and the tenure of the firm and the engagement partner into the evaluation pack.
Present the evaluation and a re-appointment recommendation to the Audit Committee, which alone appoints, compensates and oversees the auditor under Exchange Act Section 10A(m)(2).
checklist.done: an annual evaluation pack with PCAOB inspection findings, fee ratios and tenure supports a minuted Audit Committee re-appointment decision.

checklist.step: Prepare the proxy fee table and pre-approval policy disclosure
actions: Build the two-year fee table for the proxy showing Audit Fees, Audit-Related Fees, Tax Fees and All Other Fees, each tied back to the reconciled ledger extract.
Add the footnote describing the nature of the services in each category, specific enough that a reader can tell what was bought.
Include the description of the Audit Committee pre-approval policy and state the percentage of services approved under the de minimis exception in Rule 2-01(c)(7)(i)(C), if any.
Have the Controller tie the table to the general ledger and the Chief Audit Executive confirm every fee had a pre-approval before the proxy is cleared.
checklist.done: the proxy fee table ties to the ledger, carries service-description footnotes and states the pre-approval policy and any de minimis usage.

checklist.step: Handle an auditor change through Form 8-K Item 4.01
actions: On resignation, dismissal or non-reappointment, draft the Form 8-K Item 4.01 disclosure stating the date, whether the change was recommended or approved by the Audit Committee, and the Item 304 content.

Disclose whether the reports for the two most recent fiscal years contained an adverse opinion, disclaimer or qualification, and whether there were any disagreements or reportable events under Item 304(a)(1)(iv) and (v).
Give the former accountant the disclosure and request the Exhibit 16 letter stating whether it agrees with the statements, and file it with the 8-K.
File within 4 business days of the event and amend within 2 business days of receiving the Exhibit 16 letter if it arrives later.
checklist.done: an auditor change is disclosed on Form 8-K Item 4.01 within 4 business days with the Item 304 content and the Exhibit 16 letter filed.

checklist.step: Archive the independence file for the year
actions: File the engagement letter, Rule 3526 letters, approved pre-approval schedule, all specific pre-approval minutes, the rotation register, cooling-off assessments and the reconciled fee ledger into the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and confirm the record is searchable by fiscal year, service category and pre-approval id.
Cross-link the record to the proxy fee table working file and to the Audit Committee minutes.
Confirm with the Chief Audit Executive that the file is complete before the proxy is filed.
checklist.done: the annual independence file is archived under a 7-year label, searchable by pre-approval id, and confirmed complete before the proxy is filed.

testing.step: Build the population of payments to the audit firm and its network
actions: Extract every accounts payable transaction in the fiscal year where the vendor name, tax id or parent group matches the audit firm or any of its network member firms, across all legal entities and currencies.
Add accrued but unbilled amounts from the audit fee accrual account so services performed and not yet invoiced are captured.
Search the general ledger for the audit firm name in journal entry descriptions to catch amounts booked outside the vendor master.
Reconcile the total to the fee table draft and sign the population as complete with the extract date and record count.
testing.done: a complete fee population including accruals and non-vendor-master postings is extracted and reconciled to the draft fee table.

testing.step: Reconcile every dollar to a pre-approval that pre-dates the work
actions: Match each invoice and accrual to a pre-approval id and open the underlying Audit Committee minute or approved schedule entry.
Compare the pre-approval date to the service start date shown on the engagement letter or invoice, and treat any approval dated after work started as an exception.
Compare cumulative spend per category to its dollar cap and list every category over cap.
List every dollar with no pre-approval as an automatic exception and compute those dollars as a percentage of total non-audit fees to test the de minimis exception claim.
testing.done: every dollar matches a pre-approval that pre-dates the service, with over-cap and unapproved amounts quantified.

testing.step: Select and document the sample of services and approvals
actions: Take 100 percent of specific pre-approvals, all services classified as All Other Fees and all engagements of the firm outside the United States.
Take 20 further invoices by seeded random selection from the remaining population, weighted to the largest values.
Add every service delivered by an actuarial, valuation, technology implementation or internal audit practice of the firm, because those sit closest to the prohibitions.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all specific approvals, All Other Fees, foreign engagements and prohibition-adjacent practices.

testing.step: Re-perform the prohibited service assessment on the sample
actions: Read the statement of work and deliverable for each sampled service and reach your own conclusion against Rule 2-01(c)(4) before reading management's assessment.

Test the tax services specifically against PCAOB Rules 3521 to 3523: no contingent fees, no services on confidential or aggressive tax positions, and no personal tax services for persons in a financial reporting oversight role.
Check that no service amounts to bookkeeping, actuarial services on amounts recorded in the financial statements, valuation feeding into the statements, or internal audit outsourcing.
Record every difference from management's conclusion as an exception, including services correctly permitted but justified with the wrong rule reference.
testing.done: each sampled service has an independent Rule 2-01 and PCAOB 3521-3523 conclusion with differences logged.

testing.step: Recompute partner tenure against the rotation limits
actions: Obtain the engagement team roster directly from the audit firm rather than from the company register and compare the two name for name.
Recompute consecutive years of service for the lead and concurring partners and confirm none reaches a sixth consecutive year on the engagement.
Recompute other audit partner tenure against the 7-year limit and confirm rotated partners observe the 5-year or 2-year time-out before returning.
Trace one rotation that occurred in the period to the audit firm confirmation and the Audit Committee minute recording the successor partner.
testing.done: partner tenure is recomputed from the firm's own roster with no partner over limit and rotations traced to firm confirmations and minutes.

testing.step: Test the cooling-off rule against actual hires
actions: Extract from Workday every hire and internal promotion in the year into a financial reporting oversight role and every hire whose prior employer was the audit firm.
For each match, obtain from the audit firm the dates the person served on the engagement team and confirm a full annual audit period elapsed before employment began.
Check the requisition record shows the pre-offer engagement team question was asked and routed where answered yes.
Treat any financial reporting oversight hire inside the cooling-off window as an independence breach, not a documentation exception.
testing.done: every oversight-role hire is tested against firm-confirmed engagement team dates with any breach reported as an independence incident.

testing.step: Verify the Rule 3526 communication and the affiliate scope
actions: Confirm a signed Rule 3526 letter exists dated before engagement acceptance and again for the current year, and that it names the network firms engaged.
Compare the affiliate list in the independence assessment to the consolidation schedule and the employee benefit plan register and list any entity missing.
Confirm acquisitions completed in the year were notified to the engagement partner within 30 days and that pre-existing services of the acquired entity were assessed.
Check the firm's confirmation that no covered person holds a financial interest in the company is current for the audit year.
testing.done: the Rule 3526 letters are current, the affiliate list ties to consolidation and plan registers, and acquisitions were notified within 30 days.

testing.step: Recompute the proxy fee table and the Item 406 disclosure
actions: Re-add the four fee categories from the reconciled ledger extract and compare each total to the proxy fee table, investigating any variance.
Test that services are classified into the right category, particularly that consulting-type work is not sheltered in Audit-Related Fees.
Open the code of ethics at the disclosed website URL, confirm it is reachable, current and names the covered officers, and archive a dated capture.
Trace any code amendment or waiver in the year to a Form 8-K Item 5.05 or website posting and recompute the 4-business-day count from the event date.
testing.done: the fee table is re-added and re-classified against the ledger and the code URL, amendments and waivers are verified within the 4-business-day window.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the invoice or partner, the dollar amount, the rule breached and whether the auditor considers independence impaired.
Assign a root cause (procurement gate bypassed, approval obtained after work started, category misclassified, roster not refreshed, cooling-off check skipped) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date before the proxy filing for anything affecting the fee table, and require General Counsel to record an impairment conclusion for every prohibited-service or rotation exception.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarterly reconciliation as mandatory retest items.
testing.done: every exception carries a rule reference, an impairment conclusion where required, a root cause, an owner and a pre-proxy remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Audit Committee
actions: Compute the exception rate and the unapproved fee dollars against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion - auditor independence and pre-approval controls are effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with workpaper references behind each element.
Have a reviewer who requested, approved or benefited from none of the sampled services sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion and any independence incident to the Audit Committee in executive session before the proxy is filed, and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception rate and conclusion, reported in executive session before the proxy filing.
