checklist.step: Publish the close and filing calendar and lock the ledger
actions: Set the 10-K due date from filer status - 60 days after 31 December for a large accelerated filer - and work backwards to fix the ledger close date, consolidation date, draft circulation dates, audit committee meeting and filing date.
Publish the calendar to Finance, Actuarial, Investments, Tax, Legal and Investor Relations with a named owner and due date per deliverable.
Close the sub-ledgers and the general ledger on the calendar date and restrict posting rights so no entry can be made after the cut without Controller approval.
Record every post-close entry in an adjustment log with the amount, the reason and the approver.
checklist.done: the calendar is published with owners, the ledger is locked on the cut date and every post-close entry sits in an approved adjustment log.

checklist.step: Consolidate and reconcile statutory results to GAAP
actions: Run the consolidation and confirm all intercompany balances and reinsurance transactions between affiliates eliminate to zero, investigating any residual above the clearing threshold.

Prepare the statutory-to-GAAP bridge for each insurance subsidiary covering deferred acquisition costs, reserve basis differences, non-admitted assets and deferred tax, and tie each bridging item to its supporting schedule.
Reconcile the consolidated trial balance to the ledger extract used for SOX scoping so both rest on the same numbers.
Have the Statutory Reporting Manager confirm the statutory starting point agrees to the filed annual statement.
checklist.done: the consolidation eliminates cleanly and each statutory-to-GAAP bridging item ties to a supporting schedule confirmed against the filed annual statement.

checklist.step: Draft the statements and footnotes against a disclosure checklist
actions: Work the current GAAP and SEC disclosure checklist line by line, marking each requirement applicable or not applicable with a reason, never leaving a blank.

Draft the insurance-specific disclosures: liability for unpaid claims roll-forward with incurred and paid development by accident year, reinsurance recoverable by reinsurer with allowance for credit losses, investment fair value hierarchy, and the segment note.

Circulate each footnote to its subject matter owner - Reserving Actuary for reserves, Reinsurance Manager for ceded, Chief Investment Officer for investments, Tax Director for tax - for written confirmation.
File the completed checklist with the initials and date of the person who signed each line.
checklist.done: every checklist line is marked with a reason and every footnote carries a written confirmation from its subject matter owner.

checklist.step: Tie out every number in the document to a source
actions: Build the tie-out binder so each number in the statements, footnotes, selected financial data and MD&A carries a reference to the trial balance line, a supporting schedule or an external source.
Have a second preparer independently re-foot every table, cross-cast totals and check that a figure appearing in two places matches.
Confirm prior-year comparatives agree to the prior filed 10-K, and where they do not, confirm a reclassification or revision is disclosed.
Mark each tied number with the tier and initials of the person who tied it, and leave no number untied when the draft goes to the auditor.
checklist.done: every figure in the draft carries a source reference and two sets of initials, with comparatives agreed to the prior filing.

checklist.step: Run the Disclosure Committee review
actions: Convene the Disclosure Committee - Controller, General Counsel, Chief Risk Officer, Chief Actuary, Investor Relations Director and business unit leads - on the calendar date with the full draft distributed at least 3 business days ahead.
Walk the risk factors, MD&A, critical accounting estimates and legal proceedings note against events of the year, and require each participant to state anything they know that is not in the draft.
Confirm the disclosure controls and procedures conclusion under Rule 13a-15(b) is supported and record the basis.
Minute the meeting with attendance, the matters raised, the resolutions and the recommendation to the certifying officers.
checklist.done: a minuted Disclosure Committee meeting records the challenge, the disclosure controls conclusion and the recommendation to the certifying officers.

checklist.step: Receive and act on the AS 1301 auditor communications
actions: Obtain from the engagement partner the required communications: significant accounting policies and practices, critical accounting estimates and the auditor's evaluation of them, significant unusual transactions, uncorrected and corrected misstatements, and any difficulties encountered during the audit.
Obtain the critical audit matters the auditor intends to include in the report and confirm the related disclosure in the footnotes supports them.
Post the communication and the schedule of uncorrected misstatements to the board portal for the Audit Committee and schedule the executive session without management present.
Record management's response to each uncorrected misstatement, including why it is judged immaterial individually and in aggregate.
checklist.done: the AS 1301 communication, critical audit matters and uncorrected misstatement schedule are before the Audit Committee with a documented management response.

checklist.step: Prepare and sign the management representation letter
actions: Work through the auditor's draft representation letter line by line and confirm each assertion against a source: completeness of records, related party transactions, litigation and claims, subsequent events, fraud allegations and the reserve assumptions.
Collect written confirmations from General Counsel on litigation, from HR on employee complaints, and from the Chief Actuary on reserve assumptions before signing.
Date the letter the same date as the auditor's report and have the CEO and CFO sign it.
File the signed letter with the tie-out binder and record any representation the company declined to make and how it was resolved.
checklist.done: a representation letter dated to the auditor's report is signed by the CEO and CFO with each assertion supported by a written internal confirmation.

checklist.step: Protect the audit from improper influence
actions: Maintain the policy implementing SOX 303 and Rule 13b2-2 stating that no director, officer or person acting under their direction may take any action to fraudulently influence, coerce, manipulate or mislead the independent auditor.

Give the policy and named examples - withholding information, threatening to cancel non-audit work, offering future employment, pressuring on an audit difference - to everyone who interacts with the audit team, and collect acknowledgements.
Give the engagement partner a direct reporting line to the Audit Committee chair and the whistleblower channel and confirm annually in writing that no such pressure was applied.
Investigate any allegation immediately under General Counsel with outside counsel where a director or executive officer is implicated, and report to the Audit Committee within 2 business days.
checklist.done: the improper-influence policy is acknowledged by all audit-facing staff, the engagement partner has a direct committee reporting line, and any allegation reaches the committee within 2 business days.

checklist.step: Obtain the auditor's report, consent and the ICFR opinion
actions: Confirm the auditor issues both the opinion on the financial statements and, where required, the attestation on internal control over financial reporting.
Read the report for the opinion type, the critical audit matters, the auditor tenure statement and the PCAOB firm id, and confirm each matches the engagement facts.
Obtain the signed consent for incorporation by reference into the registration statements on file, naming each Form S-3 and S-8 file number.
Confirm the report date is on or after the date all audit evidence and the representation letter were obtained.
checklist.done: the signed auditor report, ICFR attestation and consent naming each registration statement are received with a properly dated report.

checklist.step: Tag the filing in XBRL and review the tagging
actions: Apply Inline XBRL tagging to the statements, footnotes and cover page using the current US-GAAP taxonomy, tagging footnote details at the level the rules require.
Minimise custom extension elements and, for each one used, document why no standard element fits.
Run the validation suite and clear every error and every warning, particularly negated labels, wrong signs and calculation inconsistencies.
Have a second reviewer compare the rendered XBRL viewer output to the human-readable statements line by line before submission.
checklist.done: the Inline XBRL passes validation with no errors, every extension is justified, and rendered output matches the statements on a second review.

checklist.step: Execute the 302 and 906 certifications
actions: Give the CEO and CFO the certification package: final document, tie-out binder summary, disclosure committee minutes, sub-certification exceptions, open SOX deficiencies and the auditor communications.

Have both officers sign the Exhibit 31 Rule 13a-14(a) certifications covering review of the report, absence of material misstatement, fair presentation, responsibility for disclosure controls and ICFR, and disclosure of deficiencies and fraud to the auditor and the Audit Committee.
Have both officers sign the Exhibit 32 Section 906 certification, which is furnished rather than filed.
Date both certifications the filing date, not the drafting date, and file the executed copies with the filing record.
checklist.done: Exhibit 31 and Exhibit 32 certifications are signed by both officers, dated the filing date, on the basis of a documented certification package.

checklist.step: Submit the Form 10-K on EDGAR and confirm acceptance
actions: Assemble the submission with the correct form type, period of report, filer CIK and all exhibits including the Exhibit 21 subsidiary list, Exhibit 23 consent and Exhibits 31 and 32.
Submit a test filing on EDGAR first, review the generated document and the XBRL rendering, then release the live filing at least 2 hours before the 5:30 pm Eastern cut-off on the due date.
Retrieve the filing acceptance notification with its accession number and confirm the document appears correctly on the public EDGAR page.
Where the filing cannot be made on time, file Form 12b-25 within 1 business day of the due date to obtain the 15 calendar day extension and state the reason.
checklist.done: the 10-K is accepted on EDGAR with an accession number recorded before the due date, or a timely Form 12b-25 is on file.

checklist.step: Report an auditor change on Form 8-K Item 4.01
actions: On any resignation, dismissal or non-reappointment, prepare the Item 4.01 disclosure with the Reg S-K Item 304 content: the date, whether the Audit Committee recommended or approved the change, opinion modifications in the two most recent years, and any disagreements or reportable events.
Send the draft to the former accountant and request the Exhibit 16 letter stating whether it agrees with the statements.
File within 4 business days of the event and amend within 2 business days of receiving the Exhibit 16 letter if it arrives after filing.
Brief the Audit Committee and Investor Relations before filing so the external message matches the disclosure.
checklist.done: the auditor change is filed on 8-K Item 4.01 within 4 business days with Item 304 content and the Exhibit 16 letter.

checklist.step: Handle post-filing errors and non-reliance decisions
actions: On discovering an error, quantify it against materiality on both the rollover and iron curtain approaches and document the analysis the same week.
Take the materiality assessment and the recommended treatment - revision in the next filing, or restatement - to the Audit Committee and the external auditor before communicating externally.
Where the Audit Committee concludes previously issued statements should no longer be relied upon, file Form 8-K Item 4.02 within 4 business days of that conclusion and notify the auditor.
Assess whether the error indicates a material weakness and whether it triggers a compensation recovery analysis under the SEC Rule 10D-1 clawback policy.
checklist.done: any post-filing error has a documented materiality analysis, an Audit Committee decision, a timely Item 4.02 filing where applicable, and a clawback assessment.

checklist.step: Archive the filing file for the year
actions: File the tie-out binder, disclosure checklist, committee minutes, representation letter, auditor communications, certifications, consent and EDGAR acceptance receipt under the fiscal year.
Apply the 7-year retention label required for audit-period records and confirm no deletion job can reach the folder.
Confirm the record is searchable by fiscal year, form type and accession number and cross-linked to the ICFR assessment file.
Give the external auditor and Internal Audit read access to the archived file.
checklist.done: the complete filing file is archived under a 7-year label, searchable by accession number and readable by the auditor and Internal Audit.

testing.step: Build the population of filed documents and supporting records
actions: List every periodic and current report filed for the fiscal year - 10-K, each 10-Q, and every 8-K under Items 2.02, 4.01 and 4.02 - with its filing date and accession number taken from the public EDGAR filing history.
Match each to the internal filing file holding the tie-out binder, checklist, minutes and certifications and list any filing with no internal file.
Extract the full set of statement and footnote figures from the filed 10-K as the population for tie-out testing.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and the number of figures.
testing.done: the filed document population reconciles to the public EDGAR history and every filing has an internal file, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the filed statements to the consolidated ledger
actions: Pull the final consolidated trial balance from the consolidation tool as at the close lock date plus approved adjustments.

Agree each primary statement line - premiums earned, losses and loss adjustment expenses, net investment income, total assets, loss reserves, equity - to the trial balance mapping and record any difference.
Trace every post-close adjustment in the adjustment log into the filed numbers and confirm each carries a Controller approval.
Confirm the trial balance used equals the one used for SOX scoping so the control and reporting populations agree.
testing.done: each primary statement line agrees to the consolidated trial balance plus approved adjustments, on the same ledger used for SOX scoping.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of figures and disclosures
actions: Take 100 percent of the primary statement lines, the loss reserve roll-forward, the reinsurance recoverable note and the critical accounting estimates discussion.
Take 40 further figures by seeded random selection across the footnotes and MD&A, weighted to the largest values.
Add every figure that changed after the draft went to the Audit Committee, taken from the version history.
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all primary lines, insurance-specific notes, critical estimates and every late-changed figure.

testing.step: Re-perform the tie-out on the sampled figures
actions: For each sampled figure open the referenced source in the tie-out binder and agree the number without relying on the tie-out mark.
Re-foot and cross-cast every sampled table and confirm figures repeated in more than one place agree throughout the document.
Agree comparative figures to the prior filed 10-K and confirm any difference is disclosed as a reclassification or revision.
Treat any figure with no traceable source, or a source that does not support it, as a fail regardless of whether the number is right.
testing.done: every sampled figure is independently agreed to source, tables re-foot, and comparatives agree to the prior filing or are disclosed.

testing.step: Recompute the filing deadline and test timeliness
actions: Confirm the filer status from the public float calculation as at the last business day of the second fiscal quarter and record the figure used.
Recompute the due date as 60, 75 or 90 days after fiscal year-end for that status, adjusting for weekends and federal holidays.
Compare the EDGAR acceptance timestamp to the recomputed due date and record the number of days early or late.
Where a Form 12b-25 was used, confirm it was filed within 1 business day of the due date and that the filing landed inside the 15 calendar day extension.
testing.done: filer status, due date and the EDGAR acceptance timestamp are recomputed with days early or late stated, and any 12b-25 window verified.

testing.step: Test the certifications and the disclosure committee record
actions: Open the filed Exhibit 31 and Exhibit 32 and confirm the wording matches Rule 13a-14 exactly, that both officers signed, and that the dates equal the filing date.
Confirm the certification package given to the officers included the open SOX deficiency list and the auditor communications, and trace the delivery record in DocuSign.
Read the Disclosure Committee minutes for attendance, the challenge recorded and the disclosure controls conclusion, and confirm the meeting pre-dates the certifications.
Flag any certification signed before the disclosure committee met or before the deficiency list was complete.
testing.done: certifications match the rule text, carry the filing date and rest on a documented package delivered after a pre-dated disclosure committee meeting.

testing.step: Verify the auditor communications and representation letter
actions: Confirm the AS 1301 communication reached the Audit Committee before the report date and covered critical estimates, significant unusual transactions and difficulties encountered.
Trace the schedule of uncorrected misstatements into the minutes and confirm management's materiality rationale is recorded rather than assumed.
Confirm the representation letter is dated the same date as the auditor's report and that the supporting internal confirmations from Legal, HR and Actuarial pre-date it.
Confirm the critical audit matters in the report are supported by the related footnote disclosure in the filed document.
testing.done: AS 1301 communications, the uncorrected misstatement schedule and a properly dated representation letter are verified against the minutes and the filed report.

testing.step: Test the improper-influence controls and the whistleblower channel
actions: Confirm the engagement partner gave a written statement for the year that no attempt was made to influence, coerce or mislead the audit team.
Sample 15 audit-facing employees and officers and confirm each acknowledged the SOX 303 and Rule 13b2-2 policy in the year.
Read the whistleblower log for any complaint touching accounting, auditing or auditor pressure and trace each to an investigation record and a disposition reported to the Audit Committee.
Confirm any non-audit fee cancellation or dispute with the audit firm during the audit was reviewed by the Audit Committee for coercion risk.
testing.done: an auditor statement, sampled acknowledgements and traced whistleblower dispositions evidence the improper-influence controls.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the figure, exhibit or filing, what failed and whether the filed document is affected.
Assign a root cause (untied figure, late source change, checklist line skipped, certification package incomplete, XBRL validation overridden) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date before the next 10-Q so the same defect cannot reach another filing, and escalate anything affecting the filed document to the Controller and CFO the same day.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's abbreviated tie-out test as a mandatory item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a pre-next-filing remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate over the sampled figures and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold for untied figures and missing certifications.

Write the conclusion - the filing process is effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references behind the tie-out, timeliness, certification and auditor communication tests.
Have a reviewer who prepared, reviewed or tied out none of the sampled figures sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion and any filed-document exception to the Audit Committee at its next meeting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception rate, a conclusion and the committee reporting date, filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Maintain the charter set and review it annually
actions: Hold the current charters for the Audit, Compensation, Nominating and Governance and Risk committees in the board portal with a version number and adoption date.

Check the Audit Committee charter states the responsibilities Rule 10A-3 requires: direct responsibility for the appointment, compensation, retention and oversight of the registered public accounting firm, which reports directly to the committee.

Confirm the charter carries the complaint procedures for accounting, internal accounting controls and auditing matters and the confidential anonymous employee submission route, and the authority to engage independent advisers and to be funded by the company.
Take the annual charter review to each committee, minute the review even where no change is made, and post the current charter to the corporate website.
checklist.done: each committee charter is current, version-controlled, annually reviewed in the minutes, carries the Rule 10A-3 elements and is posted publicly.

checklist.step: Issue and collect the annual D&O questionnaire
actions: Issue the questionnaire in January to every director and executive officer through the board portal with a 15 business day return window.

Require disclosure of every compensatory relationship with the company or a subsidiary, consulting and advisory arrangements, employment of immediate family members, charitable relationships, other public company directorships, related-party transactions and any legal proceeding under Item 401(f).
Ask directly whether the director is an affiliated person of the company or a subsidiary through control, and capture share ownership and any control arrangement.
Chase non-returns at day 10 and day 15 and escalate to the committee chair, and file every returned questionnaire in the governance record.
checklist.done: every director and executive officer has returned a signed current-year questionnaire covering compensatory, family, affiliate and legal-proceeding disclosures.

checklist.step: Test each audit committee member against Rule 10A-3
actions: For each member confirm they are a member of the board and otherwise independent, then apply the two Rule 10A-3(b)(1) criteria without exception.

Test the compensation criterion: the member may accept no consulting, advisory or other compensatory fee from the company or a subsidiary other than board and committee fees, and look through payments to firms in which the member is a partner or holds an interest.

Test the affiliation criterion: the member may not be an affiliated person of the company or a subsidiary, applying the 10 percent safe harbour and the executive officer test rather than judgement alone.
Write a per-director memo citing the questionnaire answer and any corroborating source for each criterion, and sign the conclusion.
checklist.done: each audit committee member has a signed memo testing the compensation and affiliation criteria against the questionnaire and corroborating sources.

checklist.step: Determine board-wide independence under the listing standards
actions: Apply the exchange bright-line disqualifiers: employment by the company or the auditor in the last three years, family employment as an executive officer, compensation above the stated threshold in any twelve-month period in the last three years, and material commercial relationships.

Cross-check each director's other employers against the accounts payable and accounts receivable ledgers to quantify commercial relationships in the last three fiscal years, and compare the amounts to the exchange thresholds.
Cross-check charitable contributions to organisations where a director is an executive against the disclosure threshold.
Prepare the independence pack showing, per director, each test, the data source, the amount tested and the conclusion, for board determination.
checklist.done: the board has a per-director independence pack quantifying commercial and charitable relationships against the exchange thresholds.

checklist.step: Have the board make and minute the independence determination
actions: Table the independence pack at the Nominating and Governance Committee, then at the full board, with the affected director recused from their own determination.
Record in the minutes the determination for each director by name, the relationships considered and the conclusion that any relationship considered is not material.
Record separately the affirmative determination that each Audit Committee member satisfies Rule 10A-3 and the exchange audit committee standards.
Update the board portal roster and the proxy working file with the determinations and the date they were made.
checklist.done: the minutes record a named, per-director independence determination with the relationships considered and a separate Rule 10A-3 affirmation.

checklist.step: Designate the audit committee financial expert and disclose under Item 407(d)(5)
actions: Test each Audit Committee member against the Item 407(d)(5)(ii) attributes: understanding of GAAP and financial statements, ability to assess the application of GAAP to estimates accruals and reserves, experience preparing auditing analysing or evaluating comparable financial statements, understanding of internal control over financial reporting, and understanding of audit committee functions.

Record how each attribute was acquired - as a principal financial officer, auditor, or through active supervision of such a person - and note that experience with insurance reserving and actuarial estimates is directly relevant here.
Have the board designate the expert by name in a resolution and confirm whether the designated expert is independent.
Draft the Item 407(d)(5) disclosure naming the expert and confirming independence, or explaining why the company has no financial expert, and give it to Regulatory Counsel for the 10-K or proxy.
checklist.done: at least one member is designated by board resolution against every Item 407(d)(5)(ii) attribute, with the independence statement drafted for filing.

checklist.step: Confirm the committee has authority and funding
actions: Confirm the board resolution grants the Audit Committee authority to engage independent counsel and other advisers as it determines necessary, without management approval.
Confirm appropriate funding is provided by the company, as determined by the committee, for auditor compensation, adviser compensation and ordinary administrative expenses.
Test that adviser invoices engaged by the committee were paid without management challenging the engagement, and produce the payment record for the year.
Refresh the resolution annually and file it with the charter.
checklist.done: a current funding and adviser-authority resolution is on file and adviser invoices for the year were paid without management approval.

checklist.step: Operate the accounting complaint procedures
actions: Maintain the procedures required by Section 10A(m)(4) for receipt, retention and treatment of complaints on accounting, internal accounting controls and auditing matters, and for confidential anonymous employee submissions.

Publish the channel - hotline number, web portal and postal address - in the code of conduct, on the intranet and in the employee handbook, and confirm it accepts submissions anonymously and is operated by a third party.

Route every accounting or auditing complaint to the Audit Committee chair within 2 business days of receipt with the facts and the proposed investigator, and keep management out of any complaint touching senior finance.
Report the complaint log with category, status and disposition to the Audit Committee at every meeting and retain the file for at least 7 years.
checklist.done: an anonymous third-party channel is published, accounting complaints reach the committee chair within 2 business days and the log is reported every meeting.

checklist.step: Run the meeting and executive session cadence
actions: Set at least four Audit Committee meetings a year aligned to the quarterly reporting cycle and distribute materials at least 5 business days ahead through the board portal.
Schedule at every meeting separate executive sessions with the external audit partner, with the Chief Audit Executive and with management, and record that each was held.
Confirm quorum from the attendance record for every meeting and note where a member attended only part of a session.
Where written consent is used instead of a meeting, confirm it is unanimous and filed with the minutes.
checklist.done: at least four meetings were held with materials distributed 5 business days ahead, quorum recorded and separate executive sessions evidenced at each.

checklist.step: Keep minutes that evidence the charter duties were performed
actions: Draft minutes within 10 business days of each meeting recording attendance, materials received, the substance of the discussion, the decisions and who is accountable for each action.

Record explicitly the matters the charter requires: review of the quarterly and annual statements before filing, discussion of critical accounting estimates including loss reserves, the SOX deficiency report, the auditor appointment and fee pre-approvals, and the risk oversight discussion.
Circulate the draft to the committee chair, then approve at the following meeting and record the approval.
Maintain a charter duty tracker mapping each charter obligation to the meeting and minute reference where it was performed in the year.
checklist.done: minutes are drafted within 10 business days, approved at the next meeting, and every charter duty maps to a dated minute reference.

checklist.step: Maintain the Disclosure Committee under Release 33-8124
actions: Maintain a Disclosure Committee charter naming the members by role - Controller, General Counsel, Chief Risk Officer, Chief Actuary, Investor Relations Director and business unit leads - and the reporting line to the certifying officers.
Meet before each 10-Q and the 10-K to review the draft, challenge the disclosure and support the disclosure controls and procedures conclusion under Rule 13a-15(b).
Minute each meeting with attendance, the challenge and the recommendation to the CEO and CFO.
Report the committee's activity to the Audit Committee annually.
checklist.done: a chartered Disclosure Committee meets before every periodic filing with minuted challenge and a recommendation to the certifying officers.

checklist.step: Re-run composition tests on every board change within 5 business days
actions: On any appointment, resignation, retirement or death, update the roster and immediately re-test each committee against its required size and independence composition.
For a new director, obtain a completed questionnaire and a General Counsel independence conclusion before the first committee meeting they attend.
Where a committee falls below the required independent membership, determine whether the Rule 10A-3(a)(3) cure period applies, notify the exchange promptly and document the cure plan and date.
File the Form 8-K Item 5.02 disclosure for director departures and appointments within 4 business days of the event.
checklist.done: every board change triggers a composition re-test within 5 business days, an 8-K Item 5.02 within 4 business days and a documented cure plan where composition fails.

checklist.step: Assess directors for over-boarding, tenure and time commitment
actions: Record each director's other public company directorships from the questionnaire and compare to the policy limit stated in the corporate governance guidelines.
Compute each director's attendance rate for board and committee meetings in the year and flag anyone below 75 percent, which requires proxy disclosure under Item 407(b).
Record tenure and produce the board skills matrix showing coverage of insurance underwriting, actuarial, investments, technology risk and financial reporting expertise.
Give the Nominating and Governance Committee the over-boarding, attendance and skills analysis ahead of the annual nomination decision.
checklist.done: the committee has an over-boarding, attendance and skills matrix analysis with every director below 75 percent attendance flagged for disclosure.

checklist.step: Run the annual board and committee self-evaluation
actions: Issue the evaluation questionnaire covering board and committee effectiveness, information quality, meeting time allocation and access to management and the auditor.
Interview each committee chair and the lead independent director on the results and collate themes without attributing comments.
Present the findings and an action plan to the Nominating and Governance Committee and the full board, and minute the discussion.
Track each agreed action to completion and report progress at the following year's evaluation.
checklist.done: a completed annual evaluation with a minuted board discussion and a tracked action plan exists for the year.

checklist.step: Archive the governance record
actions: File the charters and amendments, questionnaires, independence determinations, financial expert designation, minutes, executive session records, funding resolutions and complaint log under the year.
Apply permanent retention to minutes, charters and resolutions and a 7-year label to questionnaires and determinations.
Confirm the record is searchable by director name, committee, meeting date and charter obligation.
Give Internal Audit and outside counsel read access for the annual governance test.
checklist.done: the governance record is archived with permanent retention on minutes and charters, searchable by director and meeting date.

testing.step: Build the population of directors, committees and meetings
actions: Extract from the board portal every director serving at any point in the year with appointment and departure dates and their committee memberships with effective dates.
Extract every board and committee meeting held with date, attendance and whether an executive session was recorded.
Reconcile the director list to the Form 8-K Item 5.02 filings and the proxy director list and resolve any difference before testing.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and record counts.
testing.done: the director, committee and meeting population reconciles to the 8-K filings and the proxy, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile committee composition day by day across the year
actions: Build a timeline of Audit Committee membership showing each member's start and end date and identify every day on which the committee had fewer than the required members.
Confirm the committee comprised only independent directors on every day of the year, not merely at year-end.
Where a gap exists, confirm the exchange was notified and identify which Rule 10A-3(a)(3) cure period was relied on and whether it was met.
Record every composition gap as an exception with its exact day count.
testing.done: a day-by-day composition timeline shows continuous compliance or an exception with a day count and a documented cure.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of directors and meetings
actions: Take 100 percent of Audit Committee members, the designated financial expert and every director appointed or departed during the year.
Take 5 board or committee meetings by seeded random selection plus the meeting that approved the 10-K.
Add every director whose questionnaire disclosed a commercial, charitable or family relationship.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all audit committee members, the financial expert, all board changes and all disclosed-relationship directors.

testing.step: Re-perform the Rule 10A-3 independence test on sampled directors
actions: Read each sampled director's questionnaire and reach your own conclusion on the compensation and affiliation criteria before opening the General Counsel memo.
Look through to firms where the director is a partner, member or principal and confirm no consulting or advisory fee reached them indirectly.
Apply the affiliation test using the actual share ownership and any control arrangement rather than the safe harbour assumption alone.
Record any difference from the recorded conclusion as an exception, including a right conclusion supported by the wrong evidence.
testing.done: each sampled director has an independent Rule 10A-3 conclusion with look-through to related firms and share ownership tested.

testing.step: Corroborate independence against the company's own ledgers
actions: Search the accounts payable and accounts receivable vendor and customer masters for every organisation named in a sampled director's questionnaire, and for the director's own name.
Total three fiscal years of transactions with each matched organisation and compare to the exchange materiality threshold and to the organisation's consolidated gross revenues where disclosed.
Search the payroll and consulting payment records for any payment to a director or an immediate family member beyond board fees.
Report any relationship found in the ledgers but absent from the questionnaire as a disclosure exception regardless of size.
testing.done: director relationships are corroborated against three years of ledger data and any undisclosed relationship is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Re-perform the financial expert designation against Item 407(d)(5)
actions: Read the designated expert's biography and questionnaire and test each of the five Item 407(d)(5)(ii) attributes independently, recording the evidence for each.
Confirm the attributes were acquired through one of the permitted routes and that the board resolution names the person rather than describing them generically.
Compare the designation to the Item 407(d)(5) disclosure in the filed 10-K or proxy and confirm the independence statement matches the board determination.
Where no expert is designated, confirm the filing explains why, which the rule requires.
testing.done: each of the five attributes is independently evidenced for the named expert and the filed disclosure matches the board resolution.

testing.step: Test charter duties against the minutes
actions: List every duty in the Audit Committee charter and search the year's minutes for evidence each was performed, recording the meeting date and minute reference.

Confirm the minutes evidence review of each periodic filing before it was filed, discussion of critical accounting estimates including loss reserves, receipt of the SOX deficiency report and pre-approval of auditor services.
Confirm a separate executive session with the external auditor and with the Chief Audit Executive was recorded at each of the four quarterly meetings.
List any charter duty with no minute reference as an exception, since an unevidenced duty was not performed for testing purposes.
testing.done: every charter duty maps to a dated minute reference or is logged as an exception, with quarterly executive sessions evidenced.

testing.step: Test the complaint procedures end to end
actions: Place a test submission through the anonymous channel and confirm it is received without identifying the submitter and is categorised correctly.
Take every accounting, internal control or auditing complaint from the log and recompute the days from receipt to notification of the Audit Committee chair against the 2 business day standard.
Trace each complaint to an investigation record, a disposition and the meeting where it was reported, and confirm no complaint touching senior finance was investigated by that function.
Confirm the retention of complaint files meets the 7-year standard and that access is restricted.
testing.done: the anonymous channel works on test, complaint notification day counts are recomputed and every complaint traces to a disposition reported to the committee.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the director, committee, meeting or charter duty affected and whether the exchange or the SEC must be notified.
Assign a root cause (questionnaire not refreshed on a change, relationship not cross-checked to ledgers, minute omission, executive session skipped, cure period missed) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date before the proxy filing for anything affecting a disclosed determination and immediately for any composition failure.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly composition test as a mandatory item.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a stated notification requirement.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the board
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold for audit committee independence and evidenced charter duties.
Write the conclusion - governance structure requirements are met, met with exceptions, or not met - citing the composition timeline, independence re-performance and charter duty mapping.
Have a reviewer who neither maintains the governance records nor reports to a sampled director sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion to the Nominating and Governance Committee and the Audit Committee before the proxy is filed and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception rate and conclusion, reported to both committees before the proxy filing.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Corporate Secretary owns the governance disclosure calendar covering the SEC proxy Item 406 and 407 disclosures and the NAIC Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure; the Statutory Reporting Manager owns the Form B and Form F holding company filings to the lead state

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Reg S-K Item 406 and Item 407 (17 CFR 229.406, 229.407) and Form 8-K Item 5.05 for code amendments and waivers, read from eCFR, together with the NAIC Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure Model Act 305 and Model Regulation 306 and the Insurance Holding Company System Model Act 440 Form B and Form F requirements as enacted in the lead state's insurance code

In-scope processes.value: Annual proxy and 10-K governance disclosures (code of ethics, audit committee report, director independence, financial expert), the NAIC Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure to the lead state, the Form B registration statement and Form F enterprise risk report for the holding company system, Form D prior notice of affiliate transactions, and the 8-K Item 5.05 route for code amendments and waivers

In-scope systems.value: The regulatory filing calendar and submission log track the lead state CGAD, Form B, Form D and Form F filings and their confirmations; the board portal holds the governance source material and the financial reporting repository holds the proxy and 10-K working files

Compliance procedure documented.value: Governance Disclosure Procedure - the annual disclosure calendar, the source-to-disclosure mapping for each Item 406 and 407 element, the CGAD content standard and level-of-reporting election, the Form B and Form F assembly steps and the 4-business-day waiver disclosure route

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Corporate Secretary and General Counsel and reviewed by the Nominating and Governance Committee each year before the proxy season, and re-approved whenever the lead state changes or a state adopts a revised CGAD or holding company regulation

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: CGAD due to the lead state commissioner by 1 June each year; Form B registration statement due within the state deadline, commonly 15 April or within 120 days of fiscal year-end; Form F enterprise risk report due annually with or shortly after Form B; Form D prior notice of an affiliate transaction at least 30 days before it is entered into; proxy governance disclosures with the annual meeting proxy; 8-K Item 5.05 within 4 business days of a code amendment or waiver

Deadline reminders configured.value: Regulatory calendar alerts at T-60, T-30 and T-7 days for the 1 June CGAD and the Form B and Form F dates, a standing 30-day gate on any proposed affiliate transaction requiring Form D, and an immediate alert to the Corporate Secretary whenever a code waiver request is raised

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filed CGAD, Form B, Form D and Form F with the state confirmations, the proxy and 10-K governance sections with their source mapping, board resolutions and the code waiver file retained 7 years from filing, with the CGAD supporting material held in the confidential file the state statute protects from public disclosure

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A late or missing CGAD, Form B or Form F, an affiliate transaction entered before the 30-day Form D notice expired, a governance disclosure not supported by a board record, or a code waiver not disclosed within 4 business days is logged with the filing, the days late and the corrective filing made

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel approves any late or amended state filing and the accompanying explanation to the commissioner; the Nominating and Governance Committee chair signs off on any correction to a governance disclosure already filed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All governance disclosures filed in the year - proxy Items 406 and 407, 10-K governance content, the CGAD, Form B, Form D and Form F filings - together with the board and committee records that support each statement and the code waiver log

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - any state filing after its statutory due date fails, any affiliate transaction entered before the 30-day Form D notice period expired fails, any governance statement not traceable to a board record or a policy document fails, and any code waiver disclosed later than 4 business days fails

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual with event-driven elements, so the CGAD, Form B, Form F and proxy governance disclosures are tested annually after the 1 June CGAD deadline, and Form D notices and code waivers are tested quarterly because they are event-driven

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Compliance reviews the governance disclosures independently of the Corporate Secretary who drafts them and the Statutory Reporting Manager who files them; no reviewer may have drafted a sampled disclosure

Evidence location for test results.value: Governance disclosure test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository holding the filed documents, the state confirmations, the source mapping and the exception log

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filed CGAD with its supporting governance material, Form B and Form F with organisational chart and affiliate agreements, the proxy governance sections with the source mapping to board records, producible to the lead state commissioner or the SEC staff within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Lead state commissioner questions on the CGAD or the holding company filings route to the Statutory Reporting Manager and Regulatory Counsel with the Corporate Secretary; SEC comments on Items 406 and 407 route to Regulatory Counsel; both are cleared by General Counsel and reported to the Nominating and Governance Committee chair before response

checklist.step: Build the annual governance disclosure calendar
actions: List every governance disclosure due in the year with its regulator, legal basis and statutory due date: the SEC proxy and 10-K Item 406 and 407 content, the lead state CGAD due 1 June, the Form B registration statement, the Form F enterprise risk report and any state-specific governance filing.
Confirm the current lead state for the holding company system with the Statutory Reporting Manager, since the CGAD goes to the lead state commissioner and not to every state of licence.
Name an owner, a preparer and a reviewer for each filing and load the dates into the regulatory calendar with T-60, T-30 and T-7 alerts.
Circulate the calendar to Legal, Finance, Actuarial, Risk and Internal Audit so source material is requested before it is needed.
checklist.done: every governance disclosure sits in the calendar with regulator, legal basis, statutory due date, owner, reviewer and alerts configured.

checklist.step: Confirm the CGAD level of reporting and carry it consistently
actions: Determine whether the CGAD is filed at the ultimate controlling person, the intermediate holding company or the insurer level, and record the reason for the election.
Confirm with Regulatory Counsel that the elected level is where corporate governance is primarily directed, as the model act requires, and that it matches the level used last year.
Where the level changes, prepare the explanation the regulation requires and notify the lead state before the filing.
Record the election and the reasoning in the CGAD working file so the same level is used every year unless a documented change occurs.
checklist.done: the CGAD reporting level is elected, justified against where governance is directed, and any change is explained to the lead state in advance.

checklist.step: Assemble the CGAD governance framework content
actions: Describe the corporate governance framework and structure: the board and committee structure, why that structure was chosen, and how the governance framework is reviewed.

Describe board policies and practices: director qualification and nomination, independence determination, election and re-election, meeting frequency, evaluation processes, director education and the succession process.

Pull the source facts from the board portal - charters, minutes, the independence determination pack, the skills matrix, the evaluation results - and cite the source for each statement in the working file.
Have each committee chair confirm the description of their committee is accurate before the draft is finalised.
checklist.done: the CGAD framework and board practice sections are drafted with a cited board-record source behind every statement and chair confirmations on file.

checklist.step: Assemble the CGAD management and oversight content
actions: Describe the processes for appointing senior management, the suitability standards applied and the succession plans for the CEO and key officers.
Describe the responsibilities of the CEO, CFO, Chief Risk Officer, Chief Actuary, Chief Audit Executive and the Appointed Actuary, and how the board oversees critical risk areas.
Describe the compensation policy: how it aligns pay with performance and risk, whether it discourages excessive risk taking, and any clawback provisions including the SEC Rule 10D-1 recovery policy.
Confirm the description of the risk management and internal audit functions matches the ORSA summary report and the internal audit charter so the state does not receive inconsistent accounts.
checklist.done: the management, oversight and compensation sections are drafted and reconciled to the ORSA summary report and the internal audit charter.

checklist.step: Review, board-note and file the CGAD by 1 June
actions: Circulate the complete CGAD to General Counsel, the Chief Risk Officer and the Corporate Secretary for review and record each sign-off.
Note the CGAD at the board or the Nominating and Governance Committee before filing and minute the noting.

Submit to the lead state commissioner by 1 June through the state's prescribed channel with the signature of the officer the statute designates, and mark the filing confidential as the statute permits.
Record the submission date, method, recipient and any acknowledgement in the regulatory filing log and file the submitted document.
checklist.done: the CGAD is signed, board-noted, submitted to the lead state by 1 June and logged with its confirmation.

checklist.step: Prepare and file the Form B holding company registration statement
actions: Update the organisational chart showing every member of the insurance holding company system with ownership percentages, state of domicile and NAIC company codes.

List the directors and executive officers of the ultimate controlling person and each insurer, and describe every material transaction and agreement between the insurers and their affiliates in the year: reinsurance pooling, management and service agreements, tax sharing, cost allocation and investment management.
Attach the required exhibits including the affiliate agreements and the annual financial statements of the ultimate controlling person where required.
File with the domiciliary commissioner by the state deadline, commonly 15 April or within 120 days of fiscal year-end, and record the confirmation.
checklist.done: the Form B is filed by the state deadline with a current organisational chart, officer list, affiliate transaction descriptions and exhibits, and a logged confirmation.

checklist.step: Prepare and file the Form F enterprise risk report
actions: Identify the material risks of the holding company system that could pose enterprise risk to the insurers: material developments in strategy, investment or reinsurance, activities of non-insurance entities, capital and liquidity pressures, and any regulatory or legal action.
Draft the Form F on behalf of the ultimate controlling person covering each element the model act lists, and confirm consistency with the ORSA summary report and the Form B.
Obtain the signature of the ultimate controlling person's designated officer and file with the lead state commissioner on the annual date.
Record the filing and its confidential treatment in the regulatory filing log.
checklist.done: the Form F is signed by the ultimate controlling person, consistent with the ORSA and Form B, filed on the annual date and logged.

checklist.step: Gate affiliate transactions through the Form D 30-day notice
actions: Require any proposed transaction between an insurer and an affiliate - management agreements, service contracts, cost sharing, reinsurance pooling, guarantees, loans, investments above the threshold and extraordinary dividends - to be routed to Regulatory Counsel before execution.
Test whether the transaction exceeds the statutory threshold for prior notice and prepare Form D with the terms, the reasonableness analysis and the fair and equitable pricing basis.
File Form D at least 30 days before the transaction is entered into and hold the transaction until the commissioner has approved it or the 30-day period has expired without disapproval.
Record the filing date, the expiry date and the actual execution date on the transaction record so the gate is auditable.
checklist.done: each affiliate transaction has a Form D filed at least 30 days before execution and an execution date on or after the notice expiry.

checklist.step: Draft the proxy Item 406 code of ethics disclosure
actions: State whether the company has adopted a code of ethics applicable to the principal executive officer, principal financial officer, principal accounting officer or controller and persons performing similar functions, and if not, why not.
Choose and record the availability route the rule allows: file the code as an exhibit, post it on the website and disclose the address, or undertake to provide a copy free of charge on request.
Confirm the posted code at the disclosed URL is the current adopted version, and archive a dated capture of the page as evidence of availability.
Have General Counsel confirm the code addresses each Item 406(b) element before the disclosure is cleared.
checklist.done: the Item 406 disclosure states adoption and the availability route, and the disclosed URL is confirmed to serve the current code with a dated capture on file.

checklist.step: Draft the proxy Item 407 governance disclosures
actions: Draft the Item 407(a) director independence disclosure naming each independent director and describing the categories of relationship the board considered.

Draft the Item 407(d) audit committee section including the audit committee report, the charter availability statement and the Item 407(d)(5) financial expert disclosure naming the expert and confirming independence.

Draft the Item 407(b) meeting and attendance disclosure naming any director who attended fewer than 75 percent of the meetings, and the Item 407(c) nomination process and Item 407(h) board leadership structure and risk oversight disclosures.
Map every statement to its source - a board resolution, a minute, a charter or a policy - in the source mapping tab so nothing rests on drafting memory.
checklist.done: every Item 407 element is drafted with a source mapping entry pointing to a board resolution, minute, charter or policy.

checklist.step: Route code amendments and waivers within 4 business days
actions: Treat any amendment to a code provision applying to a covered officer, and any express or implicit waiver including a failure to act on a known departure, as a disclosable event on the day it is approved.
Notify the Corporate Secretary and Regulatory Counsel the same day and start the 4-business-day clock.

Disclose by Form 8-K Item 5.05 or, where the company has stated in its most recent annual report that it will use website disclosure, post it on the website within 4 business days and keep it posted for the required 12 months.
Record the officer name, the provision, the date, the reason and the disclosure route in the waiver log.
checklist.done: every code amendment or waiver is disclosed within 4 business days by the stated route and logged with officer, provision, date and reason.

checklist.step: Reconcile the disclosures against each other before filing
actions: Compare the governance descriptions in the CGAD, the Form B, the ORSA summary report and the proxy and list every difference in board structure, committee responsibility, officer titles or risk function description.
Resolve each difference by correcting the document that is wrong rather than by softening the language, and record the resolution.
Confirm the director list, independence determinations and financial expert designation are identical across the proxy, the 10-K and the CGAD.
Sign the reconciliation before any of the documents are filed.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation shows the CGAD, Form B, ORSA and proxy carry consistent governance facts, with every difference corrected.

checklist.step: File the proxy and confirm public availability
actions: File the definitive proxy statement on EDGAR on Schedule 14A ahead of the annual meeting and confirm acceptance with the accession number.
Confirm the audit committee report is furnished rather than filed, as the rule permits, so it is not incorporated by reference into registration statements.
Confirm the charters and code are reachable at the URLs the proxy discloses and archive dated captures of each page.
Record the filing date, accession number and archived captures in the governance record.
checklist.done: the definitive proxy is accepted on EDGAR with disclosed URLs verified live and dated captures archived.

checklist.step: Track state acknowledgements and answer follow-up questions
actions: Record the acknowledgement or acceptance for every state filing and chase any filing with no acknowledgement after 15 business days.
Log every follow-up question from the lead state on the CGAD, Form B or Form F with the date received and the response due date.
Draft responses with Regulatory Counsel and the content owner, obtain General Counsel clearance and submit within the deadline the state sets.
Report open state questions to the Nominating and Governance Committee at its next meeting.
checklist.done: every state filing has a recorded acknowledgement and every follow-up question has a cleared response filed within the state's deadline.

checklist.step: Archive the governance disclosure file
actions: File the submitted CGAD, Form B, Form D notices, Form F, the definitive proxy, the source mapping, the reconciliation and all state confirmations under the year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and mark the CGAD supporting material as confidential so it is not released outside the statutory protection.
Confirm the record is searchable by filing type, state, due date and submission date.
Give Internal Audit and Compliance read access for the annual governance disclosure test.
checklist.done: the governance disclosure file is archived under a 7-year label with CGAD material marked confidential and searchable by filing type and state.

testing.step: Build the population of governance filings due and made
actions: Extract from the regulatory calendar every governance filing due in the year with regulator, statutory due date, owner and status.
Extract from the filing log every governance filing actually submitted with its submission date, method and confirmation reference.
Compare the two lists and identify every filing due and not made and every filing made without a calendar entry.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and record counts.
testing.done: due and submitted filing lists are reconciled with unmade and uncalendared filings identified, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to independent regulator sources
actions: Pull the company's EDGAR filing history and confirm the definitive proxy and any 8-K Item 5.05 appear with the dates the log records.
Confirm with the lead state contact, or from the state acknowledgement letters, that the CGAD, Form B and Form F were received for the year.
Compare the list of licensed insurers and holding company members to the Form B organisational chart and identify any entity missing from the chart.
List any filing the internal log claims but the regulator record does not support as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the filing log is corroborated by EDGAR history, state acknowledgements and the licensed entity list, with unsupported claims flagged.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of disclosures and statements
actions: Take 100 percent of state filings - CGAD, Form B, Form F and every Form D notice - and the full Item 406 and Item 407(d)(5) disclosures.
Take 25 individual governance statements by seeded random selection across the CGAD and the proxy Item 407 sections.
Add every statement that changed from the prior year's disclosure, taken from a redline against last year's filings.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all state filings, the Item 406 and financial expert disclosures, and every year-on-year change.

testing.step: Trace each sampled statement back to a board or policy source
actions: For each sampled statement open the cited source in the board portal - the resolution, minute, charter or policy - and confirm it says what the disclosure claims.
Where the statement describes a practice, confirm the practice actually occurred in the year by finding the meeting, evaluation or training record.
Treat an aspirational statement with no supporting record as a fail, not a wording issue.
Record the source reference and the conclusion for every sampled statement in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled statement is traced to a board or policy record that supports it, or is logged as unsupported.

testing.step: Recompute every filing deadline and the days early or late
actions: Recompute the CGAD due date as 1 June for the lead state and compare it to the recorded submission date, stating days early or late.
Recompute the Form B due date from the domiciliary state statute - the stated date or 120 days from fiscal year-end - and compare to the submission date.
For every Form D, recompute the 30-day notice period from the filing date and compare the expiry to the actual transaction execution date recorded in the contract or the ledger.
For every code amendment or waiver, recompute the 4-business-day window from the approval date to the 8-K filing or website posting date.
testing.done: each deadline is independently recomputed with days early or late stated, including Form D expiry against actual execution dates.

testing.step: Test the affiliate transaction gate against the ledger
actions: Extract every intercompany and affiliate transaction posted in the year above the statutory notice threshold, by entity pair and amount.
Match each to a Form D notice or to a documented assessment that no notice was required, and read the reasoning.
For matched transactions confirm the first payment or effective date falls after the 30-day notice period expired or after the commissioner's approval.
Treat any affiliate transaction executed inside the notice period as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: every above-threshold affiliate transaction matches a Form D or a documented exemption, with execution dates after notice expiry.

testing.step: Verify cross-document consistency of the governance facts
actions: Compare the board and committee structure described in the CGAD, the Form B, the ORSA summary report and the proxy line by line.
Compare the director list, independence determinations and the named financial expert across the proxy, the 10-K and the CGAD.
Compare the risk management and internal audit function descriptions in the CGAD and the ORSA and list any difference in reporting line or responsibility.
Record every inconsistency as an exception even where each individual document is internally defensible, because the regulator reads them together.
testing.done: governance facts are compared across the CGAD, Form B, ORSA, proxy and 10-K with every inconsistency logged.

testing.step: Verify code availability and the waiver log
actions: Open the URL disclosed in the proxy, confirm the code loads, compare its version and adoption date to the board-adopted version, and archive a dated capture.
Where the exhibit or on-request route was elected instead, confirm the exhibit was filed or that a request in the year was fulfilled free of charge.
Read the waiver log and the whistleblower and HR case records for any departure by a covered officer that was tolerated without an express waiver, which counts as an implicit waiver.
Confirm each website-disclosed waiver remained posted for the required 12 months.
testing.done: the disclosed code URL serves the current adopted code and every express or implicit waiver is traced to a timely disclosure held for 12 months.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the filing or statement, the regulator, the days late where applicable and whether a corrective or amended filing is needed.
Assign a root cause (calendar entry missing, lead state not confirmed, source record never created, Form D gate bypassed, waiver not escalated) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date that allows a corrective filing before the regulator's next cycle, and route any late state filing to General Counsel for the explanation to the commissioner.
Carry every open exception into the next annual test as a mandatory item and into the quarterly Form D and waiver test.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, days late where applicable, a root cause, an owner, a corrective filing plan and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate over filings and sampled statements and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold for late state filings and unsupported statements.
Write the conclusion - governance disclosure obligations are met, met with exceptions, or not met - citing the deadline recomputation, source tracing and cross-document consistency workpapers.
Have a reviewer who drafted none of the sampled disclosures and filed none of the sampled returns sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion and any late filing to the Nominating and Governance Committee and the Audit Committee at the next meeting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception rate, a conclusion and the committee reporting date, filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: General Counsel owns the fitness and propriety assessment for directors and executive officers, including the SOX 402 personal loan prohibition; the HR Business Partner runs background screening and the Corporate Secretary holds the assessment record

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - SOX 402 and Exchange Act Section 13(k) (15 U.S.C. 78m(k)) prohibiting personal loans to directors and executive officers, SOX 302(a)(4) with Rule 13a-15(a) and (e) on disclosure controls responsibility, Reg S-K Item 401(f) on disclosure of legal proceedings involving directors and officers, and the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application biographical affidavit requirement with 18 U.S.C. 1033 prohibited-person screening, re-read at each appointment

In-scope processes.value: Appointment, re-election and promotion of directors and executive officers, the NAIC biographical affidavit and third-party verification for officers of the licensed insurers, background and regulatory screening, the annual D&O questionnaire refresh, the SOX 402 loan prohibition applied to every credit, advance, relocation and expense arrangement, and Section 16 reporting eligibility

In-scope systems.value: Workday holds the executive officer and director population, the requisition gate for financial reporting oversight roles and the background screening status; expense and advance data is read from the general ledger and the payroll platform to test the loan prohibition

Compliance procedure documented.value: Officer and Director Fitness and Propriety Procedure - pre-appointment screening standard, the NAIC biographical affidavit and third-party verification route, the Item 401(f) 10-year legal proceedings disclosure test, the SOX 402 loan prohibition with its narrow exception, and the annual refresh cycle

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by General Counsel and the Nominating and Governance Committee, reviewed annually, and re-approved on any change to the state biographical affidavit requirements or to the executive officer population definition

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Biographical affidavit third-party verification must be no older than 3 years at the time of filing; state notice of a change in director or officer is commonly due within 30 days of the change; Form 8-K Item 5.02 within 4 business days of an appointment or departure; Section 16 Form 3 within 10 days of becoming an insider and Form 4 within 2 business days of a reportable transaction; the annual questionnaire refresh completes before the proxy is filed

Deadline reminders configured.value: Workday requisition alerts on any executive officer or financial reporting oversight role, calendar alerts at 90 days before a biographical affidavit verification passes its 3-year age, an immediate alert to the Corporate Secretary on any board or officer change, and a standing block in the expense system on advances to Section 16 officers

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Biographical affidavits and verification reports, background screening results, questionnaires, fitness assessments, board appointment resolutions and loan prohibition attestations retained 7 years after the individual leaves office, with screening results held under restricted access as personal data

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: An appointment made before screening completed, an affidavit verification over 3 years old at filing, an undisclosed legal proceeding, or any credit extension to a director or executive officer is logged with the individual, the facts, the legal analysis and the unwind or disclosure action taken

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs every fitness conclusion and any remediation of a prohibited loan, including the unwind mechanics and whether disclosure is required; the Nominating and Governance Committee chair approves any appointment proceeding despite an adverse screening finding

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All directors and executive officers serving in the year with their appointment dates, all appointments and promotions into executive officer or financial reporting oversight roles, the biographical affidavits and screening records, and all payments, advances, credit arrangements and receivable balances involving those individuals

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - any appointment effective before screening and the fitness conclusion completed fails, any biographical affidavit verification older than 3 years at filing fails, any undisclosed Item 401(f) proceeding fails, and any personal loan, advance or credit extension to a director or executive officer outside the consumer-credit exception is a reportable breach

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is per appointment, so every appointment is tested as it occurs and a full population sweep runs annually with the questionnaire refresh; the loan prohibition is tested quarterly against the general ledger because the risk arises continuously

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Internal Audit tests appointments and the loan prohibition independently of HR and Legal; no reviewer may report to a sampled officer or have participated in a sampled appointment decision

Evidence location for test results.value: Fitness and propriety test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository, with the personal screening data held by reference only and accessed in place under restricted permissions

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Biographical affidavits with verification reports, fitness assessment memos, board resolutions, the loan prohibition attestations and the ledger analysis, producible to the domiciliary insurance commissioner or the SEC staff within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: State insurance department questions on officer suitability route to Regulatory Counsel and the Statutory Reporting Manager; SEC questions on Item 401(f) or Section 13(k) route to Regulatory Counsel; General Counsel clears both and the Nominating and Governance Committee chair is briefed before any response

checklist.step: Define and maintain the covered population
actions: Determine annually who are executive officers under Exchange Act Rule 3b-7 - the president, any vice president in charge of a principal business unit, division or function, and any officer performing a policy making function - and have the board designate the Section 16 officers.
Add the officers each licensed insurer must report to its domiciliary state and the directors of every insurance subsidiary.
Tag each individual in Workday with the covered flags: executive officer, Section 16 officer, financial reporting oversight role, insurer officer, insurer director.
Re-run the determination on any organisational change and record the date the population last changed.
checklist.done: the covered population is board-designated, tagged in Workday by category and re-determined on every organisational change.

checklist.step: Screen the candidate before the appointment is effective
actions: Commission the pre-appointment screening package: identity verification, criminal record check, credit history where the role permits it, employment and education verification, and global sanctions and adverse media screening.

Run the regulatory checks: FINRA BrokerCheck and SEC Action Lookup where the individual has securities history, state insurance department licence and disciplinary lookups, and any professional body register such as the Society of Actuaries.

Screen specifically for a conviction involving dishonesty or breach of trust, which bars participation in the business of insurance under 18 U.S.C. 1033 without written consent from the state commissioner.
Hold the appointment until every check is returned and load the results into the restricted screening record.
checklist.done: a complete screening package including a 1033 prohibited-person check is returned and recorded before the appointment is made effective.

checklist.step: Collect and verify the NAIC biographical affidavit for insurer officers
actions: Issue the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application biographical affidavit form to every new officer or director of a licensed insurer and require full completion including the ten-year employment history with no gaps.
Require disclosure of every criminal proceeding, regulatory action, bankruptcy, licence denial or revocation, and any officer or director role in a company placed in receivership.
Commission the third-party verification report from an NAIC-accepted vendor and confirm the report is dated within 3 years of the filing date the state will receive.
Have the affidavit notarised and signed by the individual and file it with the state as the licensing or change-of-officer process requires.
checklist.done: a notarised biographical affidavit with a third-party verification report dated within 3 years is on file for every insurer officer and director.

checklist.step: Test the candidate against Item 401(f) legal proceedings
actions: Ask the candidate directly about each Item 401(f) category over the last ten years: bankruptcy of an entity where they were an executive, criminal convictions other than traffic offences, court orders limiting business or securities activity, SEC or CFTC findings of securities law violation, and disciplinary findings by a self-regulatory organisation.
Corroborate the answers against the screening results and public court and regulatory databases rather than accepting the questionnaire alone.
Where a disclosable proceeding exists, assess materiality to an evaluation of the person's integrity and prepare the proxy or 10-K disclosure text.
Record the conclusion and the corroborating sources in the fitness memo.
checklist.done: every Item 401(f) category is asked, corroborated against public sources, and any disclosable proceeding has drafted disclosure text.

checklist.step: Assess fitness, competence and conflicts and write the conclusion
